text_evidence.whisper_asr: Hey TikTok, how's it going? So here we have another specimen of the Psilocybe Subraganosa. Now I don't usually see them growing this tall but I guess in the long grass it's just a different environment. So bend this guy over and you can see the gills. So you've got these darker coloured gills dropping purple spores as you can see them on the white stem or stipe. Yeah and that sort of golden coloured top. So that's a prime example of the Psilocybe Subraganosa. It looks quite like a Psilocybe Cubensis right now but we don't get Cubensis this far south in Australia. text_evidence.manual_asr:
Do you know what, guys? I found the perfect ADHD medication. Just so happens you'll have to pay 30 quid for it for a fucking 0.3 of it every time, though. Would not recommend. 
Just so Westside the brains work backwards. I'm like, what? Where did I come from? Mars? Saturn? Uranus? Uranus! Shoot us! Shoot us! You wonder why I always say I'm an alien, because I actually believe I come from Mars. Sorry. 
Anyway, back to topic. So here I am, running around, becoming bankrupt, spending money I do not have on my own brain's instability. Which I did not ask for. 
Like, thanks genetics, parents, God, Lucifer, by the sounds of it. Like, no one's got a perfect brain. But it's completely and utterly backwards in every state of the world. 
Wonder why I'm called bollocks, because everything is utter bollocks. Backwards bollocks, mate. I know ADHD works in reverse, but what? What? Like, oh yeah, it's that line, time for kippers. 
Like, what? No! I'm just sick of all these false promises from people like, rocket fuel, power there, power there, get at me power. Like, the only place I'm powering to is Bedmate for a power nap.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: This is how you feel your feelings. Okay, let's say you're enjoying your day, hanging with your new crush, everything's going well, you're vibing, and then out of nowhere, an unexpected feeling floods your body. You're all of a sudden filled with fear. Apparently, being really optimistic about your new sweetie triggers a feeling of fear and abandonment. If you can feel the feeling and let it pass through your body, then you're golden. If you can't, then disaster might strike. Okay, step one, identify the feeling. What emotion is hijacking you? In this case, you're feeling fear and worry. Step two, don't analyze it, don't think about it, don't start creating stories. Oftentimes, when you feel a feeling, we start creating narratives around it, like, I don't deserve this love, or I'm totally going to mess this up, or this has always ended badly, or my heart is going to get crushed. When you do this, you're thinking your feelings, and the more you think about your feelings, the more your feelings are going to intensify. The longer you think your feelings, the easier it'll be to add more stories about why you should feel fearful and worried, so stop doing that. Step three, take a deep breath and ask yourself where the feeling is coming from in your body. Literally, where do you physically feel it? Is it in your chest, in your tummy, in your throat? It could be anywhere. Now, sink into that feeling. How does it energetically feel? There's a specific resonance in your body. What does that feel like? Your mind will want to analyze it and think about it. Stop yourself from doing that. Close your eyes. Focus on the physical feeling. Step four, breathe into it. Send it energy. It could be healing energy, positive energy. It doesn't matter. Just focus on the physical sensation. Step five, watch it moving through your body. Does it move to different parts? Does it start to weaken or get stronger? Observe its journey. The more you watch it, the more you feel it and don't think about it, the more it'll start to dissipate. Step six, when the feeling is more tolerable, focus back on the moment with your new sweetie and enjoy your time together. You just felt your feeling. Now, repeat this the next time an unwanted feeling arises.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Have you ever noticed these pink little bumps in your skin? These are what we call sebaceous hyperplasia, and are essentially plugged oil glands. Since I had a few, I'm going to show you how I remove them as a dermatologist. I like to use topical numbing before doing it to make it less painful. Unfortunately, there's no special cream that will remove sebaceous hyperplasia completely. Next, I like to use a Cominone extractor to remove the excess oil at the base of the gland, which helps prevent it from coming back. These heal up great in about a week's time without any scarring. text_evidence.whisper_asr: This patient recently came to me with hundreds and hundreds of skin tags around their eyes, neck, and armpits and wanted them removed. So I thought about it for a while. I'm like, that's a lot of skin tags. How am I going to do this? But we figured out a way, and I'm going to show you how. And you won't believe the after results at the end. But first, what is a skin tag? Skin tags, also known as acricordons or fibroepithelial polyps, are common benign cutaneous growths found in areas of friction like the neck, axilla, or inguinal areas. They're associated with age, pregnancy, diabetes, and obesity. In the office, I typically remove these by freezing them or using sterile surgical scissors. In this case, because there are so many skin tags, I couldn't individually numb each one as that would be painful and I'd likely use too much local anesthetic. So I used something called tumescent anesthesia, which is a special mixture of diluted local anesthetic injected into a larger area using a special needle. After it was numbed, I used my forceps and sterile scissors to remove each individual lesion. And the patient was so, so happy with the after results, as you can see in these before and after photos. He felt like a new person, and I was so happy to be able to help him out.

So I thought about it for a while. I'm like, that's a lot of skin tags. How am I going to do this? But we figured out a way, and I'm going to show you how. And you won't believe the after results at the end. But first, what is a skin tag? Skin tags, also known as acricordons or fibroepithelial polyps, are common benign cutaneous growths found in areas of friction like the neck, axilla, or inguinal areas. They're associated with age, pregnancy, diabetes, and obesity. In the office, I typically remove these by freezing them or using sterile surgical scissors. In this case, because there are so many skin tags, I couldn't individually numb each one as that would be painful and I'd likely use too much local anesthetic. So I used something called tumescent anesthesia, which is a special mixture of diluted local anesthetic injected into a larger area using a special needle. After it was numbed, I used my forceps and sterile scissors to remove each individual lesion. And the patient was so, so happy with the after results, as you can see in these before and after photos. He felt like a new person, and I was so happy to be able to help him out.

The rest of you, please talk to your loved ones.

In this series, a dermatologist, that's me, describes common benign lesions you can find in your face and what we do about them in the dermatology field. This is what is called a fibrous papule, also known as angiofibroma. They're benign, common bumps that you'd find commonly on the rim of the nose that are pink, skin-colored, or sometimes red. Under the microscope, they're composed of fibrous tissue and blood vessels, as you can see right here. These aren't caused by anything you do, they just occur naturally in late adolescence or adulthood. Removing them is considered cosmetic and can be done one of several ways, using cautery, shaving them off, or using an ablative laser. They often can grow back though. Like and follow for part two, where I discuss other benign lesions on the face.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Realizations from Shrooms, part three, baby! The majority of people in this world are actually incapable at this moment of seeing reality. Let me explain. So see these LED lights right here? Let's do a little experiment. Tell me what colors you see in this picture right here. I'm guessing you probably see a lot of white and black. Maybe you're guessing this is black or dark gray, a blueish color, right? Now watch what happens when I turn on the white light. the white light. There we go. There's actually orange, yellow, with a pattern in it, and we kind of got the blue right, but it's more of a turquoise green color, right? So what that told me was me and you could both be staring at the exact same thing, literally that same exact picture. But if you are looking at that picture with just the blue lights on, then no matter how close you get to it, no matter how long you stare at it, no matter what angle you look at it from, it's going to look like just a couple colors. But then actual reality is presented when you turn on the white lights. Then you can see clearly and see it all and see all the patterns in the picture and all the real colors that are there. So in this case, if your perception, the way you see the world is the color blue, and that could represent anything. Maybe you see the world from the eyes of being really brave and confident. Maybe you see the world from the eyes of being paranoid and fearful. fearful. Whatever light you have on to see the world from, you are literally incapable of seeing the whole truth of it. You're incapable of seeing these other colors that change the picture that you are viewing. It's like that quote when you change the way you look at things, the things you look at change. This proves it. That just proved it to me. So let me know your thoughts, like for a part four, and check out my Patreon, because you would love the content I post on there.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: I just wanted to make one more video clearing the air on everything because I have gotten a lot of like criticism in terms of like the use of medication specifically GLP-1 medications like Manjaro or Zympad. I just wanted to say that I am just sharing my personal experience and I'm trying to be completely transparent about my journey because it would be unreasonable to post a TikTok about recovering from Ben GD and like losing a bunch of weight without saying like how I did it and the fact that I did need the help from medication. And what's wrong is everybody around you has the problem because they have a problem with you. But that's why they say, you have a problem. I don't have the problem. I'm fine. I like myself. text_evidence.whisper_asr: Why is sleep important for my mental health? Sleep is important for physical and mental health. Bad or not enough sleep has been found to increase negative emotions and make it more difficult to respond to stress. Sleep deprivation has been linked to depression and difficulty getting along with others. Whereas if we get good sleep, we are more creative, better at problem solving, and generally feel better. If you or a loved one are suffering, please reach out to a healthcare provider. That's Medicine Explained.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Negative thinking is one of those things that you tell yourself a story and it's a bad story and the beauty about things that are negative, they spiral downwards and downwards and downwards and it keeps going and there's almost no end to how bad your situation can be because of your negative thinking. Not looking for the evidence, not looking to change perspective, just being stuck in negative mode is really destructive. It's something that it's, we do it to ourselves a lot or we are around people that are very negative but negative thinking is not a positive thing to do. It's not a growth strategy. Negative thinking needs to be nipped in the bud. You need to look at things positively. You need to look at things forward. You need to change perspective. You need to look for evidence. Don't make up a bad ending when you don't have the negatives. It's better for you and healthier for you to look upwards and outwards and forward because that's going to give you the strength. A negative thinking really brings you down, kind of stops your growth, kind of just, it's dark and it's really overall not good for your mind, not good for your body, for your metabolism. And even for your surroundings because it is contagious in a lot of ways. So try to always take that emotion out, look for the truth, look for the evidence and look for the positive because negative thinking is destructive and it really doesn't help anyone.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: How to consume psychedelic fungi. Well, there's plenty of ways in which you can do this, such as grounding them up to powder and sprinkling on top of a pizza, shoving them in a crispy cream donut, which is one of my favorites. Putting them in a tea, jam on toast. I highly doubt it was the jam that affected the potency, so I'm not quite sure what's happened there. be curious to know what the dosage was. With the tea, though, you do have to be careful when putting them in heat because the heat can have an effect on the potency of the mushrooms, but it would really have to be pretty hot to do so. So again, it's unlikely, so you're curious to know what the dosage was. If you are looking for a potent hit, then it might be worth trying the lemon tech technique. I don't know if you've tried that one before, where you would ground them up to powder form and steep them in a mug with freshly squeezed lemons. Let them steep for a good at least 15, 20 minutes, if not 45 minutes. And then you can sieve out the remains or just chug it all down like I like to because I hate to lose any. Some say that there's no need for that, but I'd rather just make sure.

text_evidence.final_transcript: How to consume psychedelic fungi. Well, there's plenty of ways in which you can do this, such as grounding them up to powder and sprinkling on top of a pizza, shoving them in a crispy cream donut, which is one of my favorites. Putting them in a tea, jam on toast. I highly doubt it was the jam that affected the potency, so I'm not quite sure what's happened there. be curious to know what the dosage was. With the tea, though, you do have to be careful when putting them in heat because the heat can have an effect on the potency of the mushrooms, but it would really have to be pretty hot to do so. So again, it's unlikely, so you're curious to know what the dosage was. If you are looking for a potent hit, then it might be worth trying the lemon tech technique. I don't know if you've tried that one before, where you would ground them up to powder form and steep them in a mug with freshly squeezed lemons. Let them steep for a good at least 15, 20 minutes, if not 45 minutes. And then you can sieve out the remains or just chug it all down like I like to because I hate to lose any. Some say that there's no need for that, but I'd rather just make sure.

text_evidence.final_text_for_pipeline: How to consume psychedelic fungi. Well, there's plenty of ways in which you can do this, such as grounding them up to powder and sprinkling on top of a pizza, shoving them in a crispy cream donut, which is one of my favorites. Putting them in a tea, jam on toast. I highly doubt it was the jam that affected the potency, so I'm not quite sure what's happened there. be curious to know what the dosage was. With the tea, though, you do have to be careful when putting them in heat because the heat can have an effect on the potency of the mushrooms, but it would really have to be pretty hot to do so. So again, it's unlikely, so you're curious to know what the dosage was. If you are looking for a potent hit, then it might be worth trying the lemon tech technique. I don't know if you've tried that one before, where you would ground them up to powder form and steep them in a mug with freshly squeezed lemons. Let them steep for a good at least 15, 20 minutes, if not 45 minutes. And then you can sieve out the remains or just chug it all down like I like to because I hate to lose any. text_evidence.whisper_asr: Here, for example, I'm building a chat experience that is part of an outdoor adventure site. You'll see that I've now enabled the Azure AI Vision service. So now we can use video as an input for GPT-4 Turbo with Vision through the native integration of Azure AI Vision video retrieval. In my prompt, I'll ask where this destination is with a recommendation on the type of equipment required for camping in the month of January. And you can see it knows the location and based on the conditions for that time of year, it makes a recommendation for footwear and suggests additional equipment recommendations. It even recommends that I check the weather forecast to make any adjustments before my trip.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: So if you are a physician, how do you feel about your kids being doctors? Be honest. My feelings are fairly mixed when it comes to my kids potentially going into medicine when they get older. I say that because the road to being a physician is so long. And it takes that entire decade of your 20s when you're supposed to be young and living it up and enjoying your life and traveling and doing whatever before you settle down is just medical education. That's literally like all you can do in your 20s. And then when you finally get your first job at like 30, I was 32, you're not making a crap ton of money. You're comfortable. But, you know, when you're considering all of your debt, like, and then the burnout and then the fighting insurance companies and then fighting with your patients. Because if you take the time and sit down and really have a conversation, even though your time runs over with the appointment, but then everybody else in the day is mad because you ran late. But if you didn't, you're just you're just between a rock and a hard place the entire time because you're trying to do your best for all of your patients. And there's just. Not enough time in the day to do it on the flip side, I do make a pretty good living. I love what I do. I love going to work. I enjoy my colleagues and my hospital and everything. And I don't want my kids to feel like I turned them away from doing something that would have given them that joy and that fulfillment. So I want to be supportive of whatever they want to do. But I'm certainly not going to be pushing them in the direction of medicine if that is not something that they are expressing that they're interested in.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: I go in the mirror, but I'm like, Josh, you ate mushrooms. It's impossible for you to die. I turned around and I heard God say, who says I can't stop your heart whenever I want? And I instantly knew this thing just started. Like, this party just started, and I made a huge mistake. At this point, I was starting to get pulled into the spirit room. Like, I was leaving my body. Next thing I knew, I was in a hand. When the Bible says that to fall into the hand of the living God is a dreadful and fearful thing, but I'm in this hand. And all of a sudden, on my right hand, I had to see, like, 20, 30 demons. And on my left, it was, like, the kingdom of heaven. I'm in a hand in the middle of this abyss, and I knew hell was under me. It was just a dark abyss of blackness, but I knew if I got dropped, like, I was done. All these demons are on my right side. They said, he keeps coming to our kingdom and taking people out. And then he came back and ate off our table. I was in, like, the courts of heaven. Like, there was a court case happening, and I'm getting persecuted by the devil. I knew that if I got dropped from this hand, that these demons were going to, like, take me, or I was just going to drop into an abyss. I was in a hand and knew that there was nothing I could do, and that these demons were coming to get me.

Konten kamu bisa diubah atau dimanipulasi tanpa sepengetahuan kamu. Reputasi dan kredibilitas kamu dapat tercoreng. Hilangnya potensi dan keuntungan finansial dari konten kamu. Per 17 Mei 2024, nanti TikTok akan mensterilkan konten-konten yang hasilnya yang reupload. Jadi kalau teman-temannya reupload konten orang lain, persiapkan akun teman-temannya akan dadahui. Ini solusinya. Satu, aktifkan pengaturan dan privasi. Patasi siapa yang dapat menonton video kamu. Teman, publik, atau pripat. Non-aktifkan unduhan video. Tandai video dengan. Dan hak cipta. Kedua, teman-teman di videonya gunakan watermark. Tambahkan nama, logo, atau informasi lain pada video kamu. Buat watermark yang unik dan mudah dilihat. Ketiga, kamu dapat laporkan konten yang direupload. Hubungi TikTok melalui email atau formulir pelaporan. Siapkan bukti kepemilikan konten kamu. Ayo lindungi konten kamu dari reupload. Gunakan tip ini dan bagikan video ini kepada teman-teman kamu biar aman dari konten reupload. Semangat posting video setiap hari dan live streamingnya juga setiap hari. text_evidence.whisper_asr: I'm in desperate need of a gardening session because I am in the depths of hell right now, aka my ludio phase. And I hate myself, but I eat my life. So we're going to do a little gardening session. First steps are to look somewhat presentable because we're going to leave the apartments. And here's my fiance having to help me and basically drag me out. It's fine. It's fine. I feel like gardening sessions are such a process. Like, you have to have steps before and after so you're able to enjoy it peacefully. And one of them was going to Trader Joe's and getting some snacks. I am a big muncher. Like, I constantly need to be munching on something. We went to Trader Joe's and tried to get healthier snacks instead of always eating chips. I changed it to my PJs and I got my hair and skin ready for the night. So basically, I'm acting as if I'm already going to go to sleep because let's be so real. After a gardening session, the last thing that I want to do is get up and do my whole skincare routine. Like, no, I want to go to sleep. I also have to make sure that my room and my space are clean. I feel like the vibes are only right if everything around me is clean and organized. I got my snacks ready on this tray because we will be rotting from bed. That is the only place I ever want to be during a session in bed. Thank you. Why did I need four dipping options? I don't know, but I did. I love using nowadays in this house because it's quick, it's effective, there's no smell, and it also tastes great. Who doesn't like enjoying a little mottel? This literally tastes like wine. Good session for me requires good snacks, a clean space, and good TV. I need something that's going to have me constantly thinking and being like what is going on. And this is what I like to call a healthy level of rotting.

text_evidence.final_text_for_pipeline: I'm in desperate need of a gardening session because I am in the depths of hell right now, aka my ludio phase. And I hate myself, but I eat my life. So we're going to do a little gardening session. First steps are to look somewhat presentable because we're going to leave the apartments. And here's my fiance having to help me and basically drag me out. It's fine. It's fine. I feel like gardening sessions are such a process. Like, you have to have steps before and after so you're able to enjoy it peacefully. And one of them was going to Trader Joe's and getting some snacks. I am a big muncher. Like, I constantly need to be munching on something. We went to Trader Joe's and tried to get healthier snacks instead of always eating chips. I changed it to my PJs and I got my hair and skin ready for the night. So basically, I'm acting as if I'm already going to go to sleep because let's be so real. After a gardening session, the last thing that I want to do is get up and do my whole skincare routine. Like, no, I want to go to sleep. I also have to make sure that my room and my space are clean. I feel like the vibes are only right if everything around me is clean and organized. I got my snacks ready on this tray because we will be rotting from bed. That is the only place I ever want to be during a session in bed. Thank you. Why did I need four dipping options? I don't know, but I did. I love using nowadays in this house because it's quick, it's effective, there's no smell, and it also tastes great. Who doesn't like enjoying a little mottel? This literally tastes like wine. Good session for me requires good snacks, a clean space, and good TV. I need something that's going to have me constantly thinking and being like what is going on. text_evidence.whisper_asr: my sister's in town to visit and she's been craving bubblegum so bad but she ran out so I just decided to make it for her. I poured some powdered sugar on some wax paper and created a well before combining my gum base with some corn syrup and slowly melting it down. Once that was all melted I gave it a good stir and poured it into my little powdered sugar wells I created. One of her favorite flavors is green apple so I made a green apple one and then also experimented with making a cinnamon vanilla gum. Once the mixture was cold enough to handle I kneaded it and then stretched it out and made sure to always have it covered in the powdered sugar so it wouldn't stick. Then I rolled out my gum cut it into equal pieces and decided to go for a little gum ball. Once all the green apple ones were formed I moved on to my cinnamon vanilla ones and set them aside before tossing them in some more powdered sugar. To keep them fresh I placed them in some wax paper, tested the sides, and repeated that process with all of them and then they were ready to try. These tasted even better than store-bought gum and she was so excited. The cinnamon vanilla ones tasted like a donut. I was very pleased about.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: At kami nakahandang tumanggap ng alamang parusang magkasisya sa inyong kalaoban. Mba, baka nga pala mo eh makusuan mo ko sa pagdadrama. Nakakamali ka. Hindi na nyo kumalilin lang pa sapagkat ngayong panggabay palalayasin ko na kayo. Hindi ko makita pagmumukha nyo. Wala man akong karapat na makialam ay hindi ko sana magpaniwala. Hindi na kailangan gino'n. Ako pa nga ang dapat na humingi ng paumanhin sa inyo. Sapagkat nalilin lang kayo ng mga simbar kwensang ito. At mga adilang magpanggap ng milyonaryang. Hindi mo na kailangang magpaniwala pa. Nagising ka na sa katotohanan, hindi ba? Sumpayin mo na kami kung gusto kami sumpayin. Paratangan mo na kami hanggang gusto mo. At ngayon pa'y sabihin mo pinuputun mo ng namagitan sa atin. Nagkasarid dapat parusan at tinatanggap ko'y parusan yan. Hindi mo lang alam matagal na akong pinarunusan ng aking sarili. Ngunit ngayon ay natutupo at mapuputun ang panunumpat ko sa aking sarili. Ikit kong tinitimbang ang kaligayang aking natutupo. Ang ating pamimigas ng mga bulak. At ang ating mga pangarap na minsan ay naghatid sa aking lagusan. Ang yaman kong papaunin ang lahat na iyan. Ang pag-ibig at ang sisisiyang katling. Pag-ibig at ang sisisiyang katling.

text_evidence.final_transcript: So I got done with work early today. So I figured I'd make this video and show people how to properly consume mushrooms. Now, there's basically two steps to this. The first step, you want to weigh out the mushrooms that you plan to be eating. In my case, I have this big fucker that weighs about five and a half grams. That's a good one. And you got to remember, when you're eating these things, if you think it's going to be gross and disgusting, it's only going to make your culinary experience that much worse. So try to envision. yourself eating something that you enjoy. Like a nice piece of beef jerky. That's probably my favorite. And then the second step is don't be a bitch. Just eat the shit. It's only a fucking mushroom. It's not even that bad. It's a little dry. But the taste is kind of like old peanuts or some shit. I didn't mind that at all. Put that shit on my pizza. Oh, and here's a little fun fact. Even though I got done with work early today, I still get paid for the full day. So it's kind of like I'm getting paid to sit here and make this video of me eating mushrooms. Which what the fuck is better than that? Not much. And honestly, some people get nausea and shit from eating these mushrooms. I've never gotten nauseous from eating mushrooms, never gotten sick, never thrown up. So I don't know if it's more like a mental thing because of the act of eating the mushroom and you think it's really disgusting. So it like lingers in your mind and it makes you eventually throw up. I don't know. Could be. A lot of things are just mind over. matter. It's all about your perception. So there you have it. That is how you properly eat a psychedelic mushroom.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Okay, I have a terrible setup today, but this tripod isn't working. This is Matt, the Withdrawal Coach again. Just wanted to record a quick video just to talk about the experience that I had when it comes to coming off of gabapentin, the variety of withdrawal symptoms that I experienced. You know, again, I admit that I did it very poorly. I had no clue that I needed to taper gabapentin back in the day. I had only been on the medication for two and a half months. And if you have read my story on Matt in America, you would probably know that I ended up cold turkeying from 600 milligrams. And obviously, that was a horrendous experience. I wanted to just go through in this video the withdrawal symptoms that I experienced. So during that first cold turkey experience, I had no clue that I needed to taper gabapentin back in the day. I went through mainly akathisia, insomnia, and myoclonic jerks. You know, this was, of course, during this time, I had no clue what was going on. I had been taking gabapentin for post-COVID nerve pain. And, you know, for a while there, I was thinking that this was just long COVID. You know, I was just so, just, I lacked so much knowledge. When it came to just psychiatric drugs and just even gabapentin in general, just what damage it could cause in such little time. So experiencing, experienced those symptoms, it was obviously horrendous because I ended up reinstating the drug about 10 days after stopping the medication and reinstated at 200 milligrams. Still, you know, I was just doing whatever I thought was best at the time. And I felt like I was going to die. You know, like I had been on the medication for such a short period that I could get off the drug quickly. So instead of cold turkeying, I, after I kind of restabilized after a couple of weeks, you know, I tried to go from 200 milligrams to 100 milligram of gabapentin. You know, this, of course, was not a good idea. I still, you know, was not, was not sure what to do. And I really didn't know much about tapering and tapering at 10%. Of your previous dose. So ended up doing that. That's what put me in the hospital. Just, just the weight of the experience. I had a lot of mental health issues during that time as well. So ended up in the hospital again, insomnia, jerking, akathisia. I mean, these were the common ones at first. Got out of the hospital for a few days, after a few days, because of course, nobody, you know, believed me when it came to withdrawal. So I went back up to 200 and then finally, you know, by this time I was just ridiculously kindled on the medication and was just so sensitive to dose reductions that even when I did, you know, a very small reduction from 200 milligrams to, I went to 195 with just water tapering. And I started to experience, um, what I call internal vibrations and that's probably been my longest lasting symptom. I still have it, uh, to this day. Um, you know, it's just, it feels like something almost like a phone is vibrating inside of my body. I have felt it in my back primarily, um, but also in my neck and the back of my head. And then also, uh, about six months off the drug totally, I started to experience it in my legs. So internal tremors, uh, was something that I experienced pretty much, um, right after I began my slower water taper off of gabapentin. Um, again, a lot of burning sensations throughout my body. I ended up, uh, you know, getting off of the drug about seven months after I started taking it. So again, I was on it for just a little over, um, a half a year. Uh, and even... Even after, um, going off of it a lot slower, you know, I was able to stay off of the medication, but probably still went too fast tapering wise. Um, I listed out here just the, the symptoms I experienced. Burning skin, fatigue, twitching throughout my legs, visual distortions, headaches, body temperature, dysregulation, tingling on my arms, nerve pain, light sensitivity. Um, and... And like I mentioned in the beginning of this video, a majority of these symptoms have gone away. You know, I feel so much better now. Uh, almost, geez, 25 months off, um, totally. And the two lingering symptoms that I've had pretty much, uh, like I mentioned, the, the internal tremors have not gone away. Um, but I've had visual problems. Uh, a lot of visual distortions, specifically outdoors. Uh, it's almost like light sensitivity. And I just see... I just see spots just constantly. Um, so those, uh, you know, the sensitivity with my vision and then the internal tremors have been the primary two that I've experienced, uh, you know, the past 25 months. Um, but everything else has come and gone, you know, I'm feeling a lot healthier, but again, you know, I wanted to do this video because gabapentin withdrawal is just not talked about a lot still, you know, there's a lot of conversations. And, uh, support groups on Facebook, there's a lot of conversation now, you know, at least it seems gradually shifting to talking about gabapentinoid withdrawal in general with the issues with Lyrica, um, obviously as well. But again, what I'm trying to do is offer support for those who are trying to taper, uh, off of gabapentin or Lyrica, just wanting to help out to give back to the community that really helped me. Um, so again, I'm offering withdrawal coaching. And support, um, you can check out my website, thewithdrawalcoach.com I'm, uh, yeah, very excited to just work with people. I've learned so much over the past two years, you know, I really haven't read anything except, uh, you know, psychiatric drug withdrawal articles, books over these past two years. Um, yeah, I just have wanted to give back in any way that I possibly can. So again, hopefully this video, uh, might help you if you're struggling. With a gabapentin withdrawal or Lyrica withdrawal, you know, the symptoms are very bizarre. I don't want to say that, you know, it's as bad as what a benzodiazepine withdrawal would be like, but there's definitely some similarities. Um, yeah. And I just wanted to let you know, the symptoms that I have endured, uh, just to, you know, hopefully for someone else out there, who's going through this to know that, you know, I've, I've lived it, I've walked that path, lost my full-time job. Uh, but now I'm back working full-time married, uh, living a great life. So yeah, let me know if you have any questions, uh, in the comments again, I'm, I'm hoping to expand my services just to help as many people as I can, um, in coming off of psychiatric drugs. And, uh, again, I'm Matt the withdrawal coach. Thank you so much for watching and I hope you have a great rest of your day.

Parang employado lang yun, no? Late teens, had to work early on in life because nakuha akong artista and as all of you know, being in that kind of industry is being surrounded by people who do things as such, like smoke a lot. Also because of the high volume of stress and work that is placed upon you. So it was a way of coping. And it's very effective. It's like being able to tell yourself to take deep breaths. Yun na nga lang at a cost kasi may nicotine addiction. The smoke and everything that it does to your lungs. We all know that naman. So I've always had it in the back of my head na kailangan talagang makwit to at some point. But it was in my early 20s. Late na ba? Pa sa 20s ko yun. There was a campaign for stopping smoking and they got me as one of the participants. It was also a season in my life when I was getting to know God. This is probably something that God doesn't want for me because this body is meant to be His tool so something that is special that He has given me. And so why am I doing things to it that is making it unhealthy? No matter how logical that sounds. Addiction is addiction. It just wouldn't be influenced by mere, you know, oh it's logical. So it's right to do it. Then I will do it. May ako na rin siguro naisipan na to join that campaign and say yes to it. The campaign really was more to encourage others that if I can do it, you can do it also. So lo and behold, I could not do it. Hindi ko na rin talaga maalala kung pang ilang araw yun na I quit smoking, no? I was able to for a few days and then I would slide back into it and I was really miserable about it because I just, I just missed it. Madali ko pang hiwalayan yung boyfriend ko kasi hiwalayan ko yung sigarilyo ko. Kasi as in like yung levels ko ay two to three packs a day. Bago pa ako dumilat ng mata, inaabot ko na yung sigarilyo ko. Back to the campaign, I realized, I couldn't do it. Then I kept crying because I felt like I let myself down so much but more, I let God down. You should be able to do it because I'm doing it for you. After much crying, I kept asking God na please help me. Kasi hindi ko talaga kaya. Hindi ko pala talaga kaya on my own. The funny thing was I had a revelation at that point. The problem is that I'm trying to do it on my own. And the truth is, I can't. I'm right about that. I can't do it on my own. Because you know, I mean, addiction is power. It's power over you. It has overtaken you. So you need something equally, if not equally, even more powerful than that addiction in your life to actually bring it down. Lord, ikaw na to. Ikaw na yung bahala dito kasi kung ako lang talaga yung aasahan, hindi na, hindi na po tayo aabot sa finish line. From that point, for the next three days, I forgot to smoke. So I don't know, was that a miracle? I don't even know. I don't understand how I could forget. I only remembered on the third day when I kind of like snapped out of it. Shocks, ito na naman. My craving for it. But then I remembered also that there were three days na nakayanan ko just because God allowed me to experience it. And I was like, you know, that's the grace of God in my life. I'm not going to waste that. If He could do it for three days, He could do it for the rest of my life. And so, I just decided at that point, I'm never picking up a cigarette again. And I never did. From that point until today, not a puff. I would say, medyo magical yung three days. But after that nga, bumalik. I didn't get rid of the cravings completely right away. Taon-taon ang dinilang ko para mawala yung craving na yun. Kasi taon-taon nahabit din yun eh. Tinitiis ko lang kahit na nafe-feel ko. Nafe-feel ko rin naman na kaya kong hindi. So, mas pinipili ko yung kaya kong hindi. For anything, no, anything that you're trying to quit in your life right now, that's really not good for you. If you've created a habit out of it, it'll take a while before you can get rid of it. Parang taba lang yan. It took you years to accumulate that into your body. Don't expect that overnight, malulus nyo lahat yun. Point of what I'm saying here, it takes time to get rid of a habit that you've allowed in your life for a long, long time. When you're trying to quit something, don't quit too soon. Don't quit on quitting. Whenever I look back, I feel like I would've done better and I would have had an easier time. I really shifted my entire life to be healthy. Like, if I picked up more healthy habits, like if I got myself into sports, siguro, kuha kayo ng isang lifestyle. Really make it evident that these things are not helpful for your body. Kasi, kung itutuloy mo lang din talaga yung mga old lifestyle mo, ang hirap eh, diba? It just goes hand in hand. If drinking, may smoking talaga yan. It might also kind of like require you for the time being to be away from people whom you smoke with. Ano hard, right? Or maybe you could be with them but you request them for the time being na is it okay if I don't really see you smoking or something. I don't know. Kind of, severe measures if you really are serious about dropping something like this. So, yeah. That's a short story for today of how I quit smoking. And if you are on this journey, I totally, totally support you. Pagpapriko kayo. I understand the struggle. I do hope that you will tag me when you have updates of like your triumphs and even your lows. If it's a low day for you, if you slid back into the process, you are not judged. I will continue to pray that, you will have the best and healthiest life that you can have on earth. Cheers! Good morning!

text_evidence.whisper_asr: What is a personality disorder? My name is Dr. Jalil Mohamed, I'm a consultant psychiatrist and my job is to diagnose and treat mental health conditions. In order to understand what a personality disorder is, we first need to understand what a personality is. A personality is the long-term characteristics of a person which govern how they think, feel and behave. There are hundreds if not thousands of different traits which make up a personality. Some examples include how cheerful you are, how open you are, how caring you are, how stoic you are, etc, etc. When you take all of these personality traits into account, about 95% of people in a given population will fit in the middle somewhere. But about 5% of people will have personality traits at the extremes and if you have enough extreme personality traits, this would be considered a personality disorder. Because there are so many different personality traits, people with personality disorders can be very different from one another. Those differences can sometimes be classified using the personality disorder types you may have heard of, like antisocial personality disorder, borderline personality disorder and narcissistic personality disorder. Over the coming days, I'm going to be doing more detailed videos on the specific personality disorder types, so make sure to follow if you want to see those.

We're not being a perfectionist here and we're not expecting some sort of linear progression towards success, okay? The reality is there are going to be slip-ups along your journey. Stop calling them relapses, all right? They're blips, they're slip-ups. If we can learn something from them, they were very valuable. Number two is stop allowing your shame to prevent you from looking at your drug use closely. Our word of the day is curiosity, okay? If we can replace shame with curiosity and compassion, obviously, then what we can do is actually use your drug use to analyze and assess the parts of you that need healing. What are the thoughts, feelings, emotions, sensations, identity, the parts of you that are leading you to need drugs, to self-soothe, escape, numb, feel validated, okay? Assess those and pick a healing modality that actually makes sense for you. All right, number three is thinking that complete abstinence or complete sobriety is the only option for you. None of us ever wanted it, but we were told it's the only way for us to take our journey seriously, okay? I finally learned after many, many years that committing to total sobriety or total abstinence is not necessary. If meth is the thing that's causing you the most problems, then focus on removing the meth first. Don't pull the rug out from underneath you, okay? If you've become reliant on many different substances to get through your life, then what chance do you have of getting better if you remove them all at once? Focus on the meth first, stabilize there, and then you can focus on the rest in the preceding months, months, and years. All right, let's go on to our three do's today. Okay, number one, you absolutely need to start developing new tools for self-soothing, coping, and down-regulating. I'm yet to meet one person who has had a successful recovery from drugs who hasn't had to develop brand new coping tools in their life. Until and unless we find ways to manage stress, process emotions, down-regulate our nervous system, and do all that good stuff, drugs will always be a vital lifeline. Now, don't forget, you can actually do this, while you're still using, so don't let being sober trip you up. All right, number two, we kind of mentioned in the first don'ts, but we are cultivating curiosity and compassion. We're trying to extend ourselves understanding, okay? We're trying to build a large picture of coherence here. All right, what are the coherent reasons that you were first drawn to drugs and you still continue to use drugs? In what ways was it self-protective? If we do this work, we can then extend ourselves in compassion and understanding, and that's a really good base to jump off of. All right, number three is we're not expecting perfection. This is ultimately a journey that will take you time, all right? It might take you months. It might take you years. The only thing that's going to get you tripped up is if you start to think that you failed every single time you use. So we're redefining, relapse is out, all right? Every time you use drugs is just a new data point in your journey. Learn whatever you need to learn, develop brand new strategies for the next time you encounter that same trigger, and move forward in your journey. All right, please leave comments. Please add anything you want to add, help everyone else learn as well. Love you so much.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Here's how I made this video. First, I went to Ryman, went to the Sharpie section and bought a pack of Sharpie creative markers. Then picked up tracing paper and black and brown paper books and I went and bought the other materials. Using a 360 GoPro, I shot the intro. Using a tripod in place of the Sharpie, trying a few different approaches. Then I walked around in a circle, trying out different movements. And once I got the one I was happy with, I put that into a 360 Final Cut project, adding key frames to the rotation of the footage, keeping me in the center. Made that a compound clip and put it into a vertical format project, setting the clip to Tiny Planet, framing it how I wanted it to look. Exported that and in After Effects, wrote a brush myself, added a green background layer and keyed out the gray, using Simple Choker to get the outline. Now for the opening, I put lined paper over my Mac screen and traced each frame, coloring them in in an order I'd written out beforehand so they matched these Sharpie color changes. text_evidence.whisper_asr: Have you ever woken up and it felt like your neck got in a car crash while you were sleeping? That happened to me recently, and I'm going to show you a visual drill that I did to change my range of motion and get rid of my pain immediately. First, I took a range of motion assessment and I could hardly tilt my head to the right. Then I did a visual drill called gaze stabilization, where I'm holding my eyes fixed on a target for an extended period of time. This drill can inhibit activity of the sympathetic nervous system by increasing activity in the bilateral frontal lobes, as well as the fixation layer of the superior colliculus located in the midbrain. When I reassessed, my range of motion and pain had improved significantly. If you'd like to learn this drill and a few other brain-based techniques, click the link in my bio to watch a free neuro warm-up.

Interestingly, the borough of Lambeth in London has one of the highest rates of psychosis in the world. It comes as no surprise that overcrowding and squalid living conditions which can characterise urban cities are not conducive of mental well-being. Three, paternal age older than 50. But everyone's perception is unique, and we can never know what it would feel like to be you, for example. Only you know your own first-person subjective experience. I can never know it. text_evidence.whisper_asr: Internet censorship in China is actually one of the funniest things, because the government is basically constantly losing a game of linguistic whack-a-mole. Like when they first started regulating the internet in the early 2000s, they actually censored the word censorship so people couldn't talk about what they were doing. But then people on social media started replacing the word censorship with the word hóxiè, meaning harmonious, in a tongue-in-cheek reference to the Chinese government's goal of building a harmonious society. Naturally, the government then started also censoring the word harmonious, so people instead turned to the word for river crab, hóxiè. Since the difference is only in one tone, it's still recognizable even if it's spelled with completely different characters. So if you wanted to say that something was censored, you could say that it was river crab, but the craziest part is that this keeps going. Some people have also started using the euphemism aquatic product as a synonym of river crab, and it might actually be impossible for the Chinese government to ever really stop new words from popping up. A 2015 Georgia Tech study showed that it's so easy to replace sensitive Mandarin keywords with homophones that if all potential homophones were flagged in social media, 20% of all posts would be taken down as false positives. The websites would be completely unusable, which is why I don't think it would ever be possible to have a 1984-type scenario. We as humans are just too good at coming up with new words to avoid algorithmic censorship.

That's so annoying. Oh, I thought it was... Well, that's just your opinion. After that simulated argument between the two adults, the child is very aware of the new emotional context. Now watch what happens when he's given an opportunity to play again. You see, children who are exposed to negative home environments are more likely to be withdrawn, cautious, and aggressive. This is definitely reflected by this experiment. If you remember in the beginning, he was very happy, inquisitive, wanting to play with the box and see what's inside. text_evidence.manual_asr: Excuse the way I look, I look a little bit psycho, but I was just thinking it's getting colder outside now, and a side effect I don't see people talk about a lot when it comes to substance use, specifically nose drugs, is everyone, I've seen so many people talk about how they don't have like a septum anymore, like it burned the hole through, but I've never seen anyone talk about like the stages before that, so like these little like skin tags and these little like weird, it's like, I don't even know how to describe it, it's like little, this little skin tag that has never gone away since being an addict, which was over five years ago, and every winter since I've been clean, which this is my fifth winter now, it breaks open, and it hurts really bad, and it bleeds, so it's like I have a septum obviously, and I'm stretching, you know, I stretched mine, like I have a septum, but man, it was on the way, it was on the way, because I got this little, little injury in there that I don't think will ever heal. Anyone else have that?

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Can we talk about urine analysis for a second? Like, what is the goal for a urine analysis in the world of drug screening, right? Like, what is the goal of it? Now, I know all different sectors use urine analysis, right? Um, my Suboxone doctor does a urine analysis every couple of months, right? Um, and he says that it's for just transparency so he can know how to best treat me. Um, which, that I'm okay with. Because if I have a positive drug... If I have a positive drug screen for any reason, he's not going to take my medicine away, right? He's going to evaluate, see if I need anything extra, see if I need to adjust my dose, see if I need to switch things up. Um, and that's okay. But also, why do we... The reason why we need to do that for transparency is because people that use drugs have been criminalized and have been... Uh, their autonomy has been taken away for decades now, and people wouldn't feel the need to lie about their use if that wasn't the case, right? Now, clinics, right? Say you get your medication from a clinic, your methadone or your Suboxone, right? And, uh... When I first got on Suboxone, I went to a clinic, right? Um, and they did urine analysis, random. We had to go once a week. Um, and if you came up positive for a drug screening, you were immediately on a three-day fast taper, what does that do? That throws people back into... Using from the illicit supply. And now, they're at a higher risk for overdose. So, you drug test somebody, you see that they are positive, and then you take away the one thing that's helping them. That makes absolutely no fucking sense to me. Now, let's say you're on probation. Or, parole, right? Um, which is already a fucked up system within itself. Like, a lot of the times people are coerced into just parole because no one wants to just sit in fucking jail or prison. Of course, you want to be able to get out, but you're still under constant surveillance, and you can just be thrown back in jail for doing just regular ass things. Um, but... Using substances is one of those things. Uh, they use it for surveillance, and just so you can just toss someone back in jail, like, I just don't understand. And, I mean, we're not even gonna get into the fact that, like, so many times there are false positives, but who are they gonna believe? Like, the person that... That has substance use disorder, who has been struggling with substance use, or, uh, what the urine analysis cup says. Nine times out of ten, they're gonna believe that cup over the human being, uh, themselves. Um, I just feel like a lot of the times, urine analysis is a way to take someone's autonomy away, to let them know that you don't trust them. And, tch... You know, it's just a means of control and power. Like, people wouldn't have to lie and be shady and, like, you know, do all these crazy things to get a negative result on their urine analysis if they were just treated like human beings, and if using substances wasn't criminalized. Um... Like, all of this wouldn't be necessary, and it's really not fucking necessary. Um, yeah, that's just what I was thinking about today. Uh, let me know your thoughts. Alright, love you, bye!

text_evidence.whisper_asr: malditos demonios que se revelaron en medio de las llamas en California. California está envuelto en llamas debido al incendio más grande de su historia. Casas y edificios han sido arrasados, cientos de personas están desaparecidas, millones han sido desplazadas y muchas vidas se han perdido. En este video verás diferentes áreas y tomas que, según testigos, muestran caras parecidas a demonios entre las llamas y el humo. Un grupo de personas asegura haber visto estas figuras demoníacas mientras huían para salvar sus vidas, dejando atrás todo lo que tenían, sus hogares, carros, ropa, absolutamente todo. Nadie podía escapar en carro ni en bicicleta, solo a pie. Mientras corrían, cuentan que veían las inmensas llamas que parecían alcanzar el cielo y entre ellas surgían rostros aterradores con forma de demonios. Incluso algunos bomberos han declarado haber sido testigos de estos fenómenos. Es algo asombroso y perturbador a la vez, un suceso que para muchos confirma lo que ya está escrito en la Biblia, que en los últimos tiempos los demonios se revelarán ante la humanidad. Este incendio y las extrañas apariciones son interpretados por algunos como una señal apocalíptica. Cristo viene, comparte este mensaje con alguien que esté apartado de Dios o que no lo conozca para que se arrepienta y busque a Cristo antes de que sea demasiado tarde. Cristo viene

And then in 2014, the U.S. Senate approved a military spending bill that included the Oak Flat land swap, which gave the land to Resolution Copper. The legislation also overturned the historic 60-year mining ban previously enacted to protect Oak Flat's wetland and wildlife. For the Apache people, we believe it's a violation of our religious freedom because this mine will cause a two-mile-wide estimated crater as deep as the Eiffel Tower. Everything will be gone forever. We cannot practice our traditions, our culture, and do our spiritual beliefs in prayer. In March of 2024, a federal appeals court ruled in favor of the mining giant. The court rejected the Apache Stronghold's appeal that the land transfer would violate their rights under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act. Now they are fighting at the Supreme Court level. They are asking the Apache to reclaim their land from corporate control. And it is to the fight and the resiliency of my ancestors that I am here today. The struggle for Native peoples still continues. We constantly are the dust underneath the carpet in this country, where our environment is being destroyed. Our religious freedom is being taken away and threatened. If it wasn't for the boarding school era, then it was the Relocation Act. And if it wasn't for that, it is the current issues, the violations of our mother fear.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Today, I entered Fortnite to see that Reload had altered its weapon pool. What in Queen Elizabeth's crumpets is this update? To determine the faultiness of this update, I had to get a first-hand experience with the arsenal. I can sense this conniving rat on my radar. Shut on! This geezer bared a Desert Eagle just for me. Thank you, mister. The next plonker must have been utterly unaware of my impeccable aim. Back to the lobby, nitwit! I continued to wipe away the crust of this match, but the slaughter left me impaired. I was luckily able to locate an air package, but upon its opening, may have laid out some of the most piss-poor pitiful loot I have ever seen in my life. Let's analyze what we've got here. To start off, I was given an uncommon heavy shotgun and pistol. I didn't know Epic Games was already celebrating St. Patrick's Day. Previewing further footage shows a rare AK was dropped as well. Do they think I am a part of the fucking Smurf Taliban or something? Goodness ever-loving, gracious Fortnite. Trying to forget this traumatizing treasure, I got back into my regularly scheduled plonker plowing. And for this elimination, I'll let the gameplay explain itself. Jesus fucking Christ, can we get a post-match replay on that? I hold the stare edit for a moment to gather my thoughts. And within a goddamn picosecond of releasing the edit, I reset it. Successfully squandering my opponent's shotgun blast, which then leaves me with a benignant opportunity to strike them down. I am the Fortnite Da Vinci. Don't you dare think about escaping, buddy. Mwahahahaha! Mwahahahaha! You're friggin' burnt toast! What? Die, you evil gimp suit lady! Good thing I'm safe now. Scheisse! For Venton's Eden called Scholarly Fish.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: The man accused in the death of a 15 year old boy is booked in the Winnebago County Jail after being arrested in Georgia. 34 year old Matthew Alexander is charged with drug induced homicide. He was arrested last month by Clayton County Sheriff's deputies in Forest Park, Georgia. In July 2024, Rockford police responded to Van Wee Avenue for reports of an overdose death. According to court documents, the teen victim's phone contained texts about purchasing drugs from Alexander. An autopsy revealed the victim died of a drug overdose. Alexander was booked in the county jail yesterday and is awaiting a pretrial release here.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: We always want things to happen so fast, so one of the questions we get a lot is, how long does it take to see results from skincare? Here's the truth. Think of your skin like a garden. Plants don't grow overnight and neither does healthy skin. On average, skin cells need about 28 days to renew. For active products like retinol, you might notice smoother texture in a month or so, but building collagen can take an extra few months. Stick with it for at least 12 weeks before deciding if something is working for you or not. you

text_evidence.whisper_asr: We've all got that vape bean friend who hoards more empty carts than a grocery store parking lot and he uses Nick. So I slapped together an analog lung to demonstrate how dense vapor is and show that it can, in fact, recondense in our warm lung. I'm serious, the guy flies for work and then zeros or ghosts every puff throughout the flight. To which he responds, well, the bathroom has sensors. Long story short, I finally convince him to go to an herb shop and get some mullin, get some elderberries, ginger, and make an herbal tea with those ingredients. text_evidence.whisper_asr: Ms. Murray, you're recognized. Thank you. Very nervous. Thank you for this opportunity to speak today. My name is Gretchen Murray, and Gage's Law is named for my son. He was 29 years old when he was poisoned with fentanyl on September 26th of 2022. I'll share just a few of the events that's led me here today and to advocate for this bill. In my son's circumstances, the hospital did not test for illicit fentanyl in the ER, nor the whole time he was there. After he passed away, he was sent to the medical examiner for an autopsy. We waited approximately 60 days for the autopsy and toxicology results in hopes for law enforcement to pursue homicide charges. During the autopsy, the medical examiner misinterpreted medication orders and thought that fentanyl had been administered. After it was ordered to conduct an assessment which tests function of the brain. This was without having any confirmation of the illicit fentanyl already in his system. As a result, the medical examiner could not determine if the fentanyl in my son's blood at autopsy was from the illicit source or from the hospital. This prevented law enforcement from charging death by distribution and our assistant state attorney from being able to prosecute for my son. For 10 months, I wondered why the hospital would have given more fentanyl without testing him first. I wondered if what they gave him pushed him beyond being able to survive. I then lodged a complaint with the Joint Commission to get answers. I was contacted by the hospital letting me know that they received the Joint Commission request and would be in contact with to set up a meeting with me after their investigation was complete. I started to prepare. There was only with a timeline of events for this meeting. Combing through all the records, it was then that I discovered that the assessment had not been completed and the orders for fentanyl were never signed off as being administered. I later confirmed with the hospital that fentanyl was not given. A week later, the medical examiner amended the autopsy report and the death certificate for us. Law enforcement was then able to pursue homicide charges. Soon after, the state indicted both men for first-degree capital murder by distribution. Both have been incarcerated since December 6th of 2023, and the first trial is set to be April 28th. This bill could have prevented almost a year lost during my son's death investigation. It also would have allowed law enforcement to seek attempted murder charges on behalf of my son's friend who survived. Testing will also prevent hospitals from potential medical misfeasance when administering fentanyl in cases of overdoses or poisonings. Initial testing will also prevent non-fatal overdoses from being discharged from the hospital without confirmation that they ingested illicit fentanyl. Testing will also firm up the number of overdose cases in Florida. This bill will save lives. I'm so grateful for your time today. Thank you. Thank you, Ms. Murray. And then I mainly smoke guards. But I'm telling you, when I cop a motherfucking zip, I'm not smoking no guard, unless I'm double-eyed them, bitch. But yeah, at smokers, we definitely need to learn how to preserve our shit.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Hey gardening besties. Your fairy gardening mother is freaking tired. So let's wake up with a little bit of stevia in our coffee, if you know what I mean. And of course we have to start our session by squeegeeing the gardening globe. Squeegeeing, is that a word? I mean, we've got to be able to see our future clearly, right? I finally have a day off so I can let my creative channels open up and I can start working on finishing my mushrooms for my gardening globe. A lot of you are asking about mold and mildew. This is an outdoor rug. Nothing in here is going to get dank. A mildewy. I did hate those pool noodles, though. I put them up completely wrong anyway, so I went ahead and pulled those down. I have some extra poles, so I'm going to replace the poles that I had in there because user error. And hopefully the majority of the April showers have passed. Although it's drizzling this morning, and it's freaking cold. And just to prove that to you guys. There's 90% humidity out here, and it's about 48 degrees. And of course, it's perpetually 420, right? Yeah, you know it. So I'm in West Virginia, and we have. have legal, medical. I had to show you my nails. Got my nails done yesterday at a magical place called Bloom Beauty Bar in downtown. Historic Charleston, West Virginia. Love them. But Hillfire is a West Virginia-owned company, locally grown, source. Freaking love them. I don't know if they have a TikTok. Anyway, you know the drill. It's 420 somewhere. Go freaking celebrate. And just remember, your fairy gardening mother freaking loves you, okay? You have value, you have worth. Go fucking live your life.

text_evidence.final_transcript: Hey gardening besties. Your fairy gardening mother is freaking tired. So let's wake up with a little bit of stevia in our coffee, if you know what I mean. And of course we have to start our session by squeegeeing the gardening globe. Squeegeeing, is that a word? I mean, we've got to be able to see our future clearly, right? I finally have a day off so I can let my creative channels open up and I can start working on finishing my mushrooms for my gardening globe. A lot of you are asking about mold and mildew. This is an outdoor rug. Nothing in here is going to get dank. A mildewy. I did hate those pool noodles, though. I put them up completely wrong anyway, so I went ahead and pulled those down. I have some extra poles, so I'm going to replace the poles that I had in there because user error. And hopefully the majority of the April showers have passed. Although it's drizzling this morning, and it's freaking cold. And just to prove that to you guys. There's 90% humidity out here, and it's about 48 degrees. And of course, it's perpetually 420, right? Yeah, you know it. So I'm in West Virginia, and we have. have legal, medical. I had to show you my nails. Got my nails done yesterday at a magical place called Bloom Beauty Bar in downtown. Historic Charleston, West Virginia. Love them. But Hillfire is a West Virginia-owned company, locally grown, source. Freaking love them. I don't know if they have a TikTok. Anyway, you know the drill. It's 420 somewhere. Go freaking celebrate. And just remember, your fairy gardening mother freaking loves you, okay? You have value, you have worth. Go fucking live your life.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Three reasons. Zah is better than alcohol. Number one. Zah doesn't ruin families. Someone had to say it. And I'm talking from personal experience here. Alcohol is one of the main disruptors of many marriages and relationships. Truth be told, nobody's broken up over some pot. Unless you're like 14. Number two, I can still be productive off of the Zah. You get a couple drinks inside of me? And I ain't doing shit. I'm not doing anything when I'm drunk. Zah is almost a medicine. It helps me get a little creative. It gets the juices flowing when I'm not stoned, that is. Alcohol does none of that. The moment liquor enters my body, I'm not doing anything. Vacation mode enabled. And finally, number three, Zah doesn't make me feel like shit in the morning. Alcohol, completely different story, okay? The next morning after I drink a ton, I usually feel like I just gave birth to three oversized infant child. My body went through it and I don't know what the hell happened. How could I possibly feel like this? Yeah. Zah, you don't feel any of that. If anything, you feel great the next morning. Guys, let me know in the comments which one you like better. Zah or alcohol? For me, the option is pretty easy. And guys, drop a life for more.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Two grams of mushrooms in this protein bar. Like, what? This is the shroom bar. It's kind of small. Cheers. Okay, it tastes pretty good. Four different types. Fortyceps, Rishi, Lines Mains, and Turkey Tail? That's interesting. More of a dark chocolate peanut buttery taste, but not bad. Maybe those are the mushrooms. I don't really know what they look like. Now we're getting cacao nips or chocolate chips. Those are delicious. I've reviewed 400 plus proteins and never have I ever had a mushroom protein bar. Super unique. Taste-wise, it's like an 8 out of 10, pretty good. The mushrooms are there to boost focus, energy, and mental clarity. I don't know if all experiencing any of those effects, but we'll see. Overall, I'm going to give this bar an 8.2 out of 10. I think they're on sale in the TikTok shop down below. Let me know what I should try next. I'll see you all tomorrow. Follow for more protein reviews and peace.

text_evidence.final_transcript: Two grams of mushrooms in this protein bar. Like, what? This is the shroom bar. It's kind of small. Cheers. Okay, it tastes pretty good. Four different types. Fortyceps, Rishi, Lines Mains, and Turkey Tail? That's interesting. More of a dark chocolate peanut buttery taste, but not bad. Maybe those are the mushrooms. I don't really know what they look like. Now we're getting cacao nips or chocolate chips. Those are delicious. I've reviewed 400 plus proteins and never have I ever had a mushroom protein bar. Super unique. Taste-wise, it's like an 8 out of 10, pretty good. The mushrooms are there to boost focus, energy, and mental clarity. I don't know if all experiencing any of those effects, but we'll see. Overall, I'm going to give this bar an 8.2 out of 10. I think they're on sale in the TikTok shop down below. Let me know what I should try next. I'll see you all tomorrow. Follow for more protein reviews and peace.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Whenever somebody find out that a mom is a garden mom, they try to just avoid the elephant in the room. I know y'all got that number one question. How do you do it? Bitch, let me break it down for you. Actually, let me break it down for all of us, because I know I ain't standing alone. We do it just like anybody else. We all tend to confuse gardening with them other sports. We ain't in the big leagues, bitch. We just in our own league. We do everything just as normal as any other motherfucker who ain't gardening. Only thing that that gardening does for me is make me a lot more happy. A little bit more hungrier, a lot more productive, a lot more motivated, little less on edge. Comfortable, bitch. I like to be fucking comfortable, don't you? Oh, y'all wait till 5 o'clock, but then when it ain't 5 o'clock, y'all say it is 5 o'clock somewhere, so you got your justification. But I'm supposed to just be sitting around this bitch shit out of luck. Pth, you're thaw. I'm a garden a little bit here. I'm gonna go outside and I'm a garden there. I'm a garden again, bitch, and you're gonna mind your motherfucking biz. Ain't no elephant in the room. You're just so deep in our business, you can't help but wonder how. How the fuck do they do it all? They're so bad ass. Y'all, and we is, we been new. Y'all gonna quit. Counting us out. And if you continue to count us out, guess what? We don't give a fuck because we in that garden. I can't tell you what to do, but just know I'm happy over here, baby. We all is, trust. But that's the business of ours. You need to go find your own. Until next time, love you guys.

Before I talk a little bit about that, though, I did want to mention how, you know, there are countless individuals out there who don't make it through psychiatric drug withdrawal. And it's an injustice. It is a crime against humanity. And I think that we have to acknowledge that. But the thing is, is that if you make it through psychiatric drug withdrawal, you are untouchable. You are able to accomplish anything that you set your mind to, because you've been through hell. Not just for a few days, but most of the time, months and years, and daily just choosing to get up and continue to fight. So I just wanted to make this encouraging video and just say that if you make it through this, you can do anything. You can overcome anything. Just make it through. Just make it through. Just meditate on that.

text_evidence.final_transcript: Let's go to Disneyland. I'm really excited because I get to eat the foods that I want to eat and the drinks that I want to drink and I haven't done so in quite a while. So this is like a last hurrah, if you will. But we did a little bit of a cold start. She's ready. So, cheers. Here's my outfit. Pocus pocus. And I'm wearing these. I'm going to try to try. to force myself to go on rides that I normally don't like and to do them by myself. So that means waiting in line by myself with me, my own thoughts, and people's conversations around me. The voices! Anyways, see you guys, because I'll be vlogging.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: I'll just get ready. And try to beat the gummy. Yes, we are back with your favorite series, but also my hair is herring today. I'm over 21 and live in California, but you guys always ask me what brand this is. It's Leu. I don't know exactly how to say it, but I'll tag them. If you have a favorite garden gummy brand, can you please post it in the comments? I'm looking for some new good ones to try. I haven't tried the Anastasia Luminous Foundation in forever, so let's give it a try. This is a bit too dark for me. This color's a bit too dark for me, so we're going to use our givon sheet corrector. It has like blue and white pigments mixed in together, so it should. lighten things up a tiny bit. You can just see as I apply it here. I'm so excited for this to hit too because my husband and I have plans to watch Squid Game tonight. We are finally catching up on season two. Definitely need a lighter shade of this, so ignore the color. If you're a TV show watcher, what's your favorite TV show right now? Because all of our favorite shows are coming back in full swing like you, I think, is about to drop if it hasn't already. So I got a wee bit distracted and I tried on some new cover girl products. I made a separate video on it, so stay tuned for that. I'm going to use the Rare Beauty Setting Spray. Going back to favorite TV shows, I am so excited for Handmaid's Tale. We're waiting until most of the season is done for us to watch it, so no spoilers. So I know I'm usually doing my makeup while filming these videos, but someone in my comments posted the idea of doing beat the gummies, but with other things, specifically around doing my skincare at night because my skincare routine is long. Why I just said it like that, I do not know. I feel like it could be a series, like beat the gummy with anything, right? Like try to clean the house before or whatever. what are other tasks you can do? Do you ever have those times where you think of something in your head and it happens, or like you're thinking of a specific word that doesn't get said a lot or isn't spoken out loud a lot? And then all of a sudden someone says that word in a sentence and you're like, I was just thinking that. That happened to me the other day and I blew my mind, but like, you're not going to say I was thinking that word. That's a weird thing to say, right? Am I already toasty or is this just my ADHD brain going wild? I don't know if I like what I did there, but it's there. I'm all of a sudden craving a white claw right about now too. That sounds really good. Do I have those downstairs? Yeah, I do. You hear that? My cat is standing on my speaker. This one causing all the problems. Hello. Let's use a little rare beauty. Love this freaking product. I'm adding... I'm adding a little bit into my crease too so the look is all tied together. You can tell, a little bit of pinky there. Heartlit tubing Excel mascara. Every time I make one of these videos, I feel like I am all over the place. Let's finish things off with a pink lip gloss. This one is from Kiko. And this is the finished look. Dude, I'm so hungry right now, so I'm gonna go. Bye!

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Let's walk through how to draw medications into a syringe. First up, you'll need a syringe to hold the volume of the dose in milliliters, a blunt needle, an alcohol swab, and a needle for administration if you're giving it by injection. First, you want to attach the blunt needle to the syringe. Once we've done all our medication checks, you can pop the top of the medication vial off. Now, draw the air back the same dose that you'll be administering. So here we'll give 2.5 milliliters, so we'll want to pull back 2.5 milliliters of air. Then you can clean the top of the vial with an alcohol swab. Then insert the blunt tip needle into the center of the vial's rubber stopper and inject 2.5 milliliters of air. Now, flip the vial with the needle inside and pull your needle down a little bit. This will help the tip of the needle to sit in the actual fluid and helps you avoid pulling back air that sits on top of the vial. So again, the bevel or the tip of the needle should sit right in that fluid. Draw the full dose back, being sure to retract the entire ordered dose. Now, hold the syringe upright to level out the fluid and push the plunger to expel any air that remains on top. Be sure to remove the blunt tip needle and either attach your injection needle or attach the syringe to the IV port if you're administering it intravenously. That's all for drawing up medications. Happy studying, future nurses.
