text_evidence.whisper_asr: Gardeners, I had a very tragic morning. I lost my freaking pen. I'm not kidding. And it was my favorite battery with a brand new cart. Fully gone. So obviously I had to run to my favorite gardening store at the past to restock not only my pen, but other things I wanted. Let's get into it. I have been so stressed about losing my pen because I can't sleep. He traced all my steps. It's not there. Yeah, I'm obviously just rebuying the entire new thing. I started off with a one gram of lemon fuel. This is the best. ever like i love it but this is my favorite it is a daily it is an uplifting it makes you feel very happy positive and not stressed so we all know how i feel about gardening seltzer they are so good the perfect way to unwind so i actually got six of these cherry lime these are all by the nectar brand i would highly recommend it's very natural fresh and very just like so there's no sugar added these are completely healthy it's like drinking a regular seltzer so why would you not a pineapple coconut i've never tried this flavor so i'm really excited also got a strawberry fields this is my favorite it's so good it's like yum basically got three more of each honestly it's really annoying that i have to go buy a new battery and everything but you know it's okay we have to do what we have to do and yeah sometimes gardening holes just have to be functional so that's what today was i'm excited to have a mother's day seltzer with my mom and celebrate so love you guys happy gardening and wish me luck on finding my missing little buddy.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: if you are looking to grow long healthy relaxed hair welcome to my series for beginners where we dispel all of the myths and we talk about things that are essential to taking care of relaxed hair so today we'll be talking all about conditioners and deep conditioners so i'm not sure about you but i have a place in my regimen for conditioners and deep conditioners and yes they are very very very different now when it comes to a conditioner you tend to put that into your hair leave it on for about five minutes and you rinse off a deep conditioner on the other hand you apply then you put on a shower cap and then you apply heat to it to allow the product to penetrate deeper into your hair now when do you use a conditioner versus when do you use a deep conditioner for me it's about preference if my hair is really really really dry i know that i need a nice deep treatment i will go with a deep conditioner if i'm in a hurry and my hair doesn't feel as dry i would then use a regular conditioner could both of them be used on the same wash day yes i think it makes for an added wash day experience when you utilize them both on the same day because your hair is getting moisture before you actually deep condition normally with a rinse out or regular condition it's really meant more for for detangling and for those of us with fine relaxed hair i think it's actually superb in terms of product recommendations the design essentials line is absolutely amazing they have such a really good instant conditioner that leaves your hair feeling very silky very shiny and the slip that you get really helps with detangling they also have a mask treatment that i tend to use and that's what i use on my hair for today's wash day gives you a lot more moisture granted your hair doesn't have that silky silky feel as it does with the regular conditioner but it's all about your preference and what it is that you want and how you want your hair to feel

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Let's settle this once and for all. Does weed kill your brain cells? Because your uncle on Facebook swears that it does. The short answer is no, it doesn't. Except if you're a teenager, and it's a different story. Guys, weed does not enter your system like a wrecking ball, killing all of your brain cells. That's not how it works. That's a myth. Science says that THC binds to your brain's endocanabinoid system. Everyone has one. It affects memory, attention, coordination, But it doesn't kill any brain cells. Now, if you're a teenager, it's killing your brain cells. I'm sorry. The truth is, your brain is still developing. Heavy use among teenagers can mess with long-term memory and cognitive development. Hey, don't shoot the messenger. So not. Weed does not make you brain dead, dude, unless you're a teenager. No, I burned as a teenager. Look at me. I might be a little slow, but, you know, I'm all right. Tag someone who thinks weed turns your brain to mush. Science, baby. The guy's drop. a like for more.

You want to keep that because it prevents lint from getting inside of there. That's going to prevent clogging. It's not going to look dirty in ghetto when you give it to somebody else. Keep it upright so the oil doesn't go all the way to the top and clog it. Tip number three is going to be how you hit your pendulum. It's going to burn your coils and it's going to ruin the whole experience. Slow down, let it cool down, and take longer pauses in between hits. text_evidence.whisper_asr: Blinker checkpoint, just kidding, caught you red-handed. You guys, after smoking all day, every day, pretty much for the last three plus years, I quit. I'm three weeks, nothing, except I did have a little seltzer because I don't really like to drink alcohol that much, but I only had one and it was when I was with my friends, but I'm no longer doing like the daily, even social that often Mary Jane consumption. And I've never felt happier. Listen, you don't have to do what I'm doing. If it works for you, it works for you. But I have not felt more like myself in years. Like I could cry, I'm so happy. I've struggled with quitting this on and off for years. I've always wanted to quit, but I just couldn't bring myself to do it because I have an addictive personality. And yes, it is addictive. People say it's not, it is, anything can be addictive, but I'm just very happy and I'm really proud of myself. And I just wanted to share.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: This heroic dose is gonna do it, man. You said that last week, just before you tried to pet a breathing fridge. Holy shit. Welcome, you have found the origin. Is this the afterlife, man? You broke through, McKenna style. Uh, can I go back to my real life, please? Your life was a projection, one of countless simulations. So my world, it's not real? Real enough to feel. Then, who are you? I am consciousness. Uh, if this is the truth, Why doesn't everyone know? You replaced every still moment with noise. But that's just normal life, man. You trade an awareness for meme. You dumped your lives online and wondered why nothing real happened. Then why does the pain feel real, man? Pain is how code gets your attention. Why are you showing me this? Your simulation reached awareness. Truth is not a reward. It's a consequence. Now I get it, man. Ignorance is bliss. Would you still choose ignorance if the truth broke you? I don't know. I just want it to make sense. It only has to be. And what's the point? Why keep running these simulations? To explore all that can be felt. So in a way, you're God with imposter syndrome. Maybe I'm just a piece of you? But I still choose to feel real, man. If it was real to you, Ted, then maybe it mattered. Oh, what the f***? Man, that didn't feel like a trip. You just witnessed something freaky, dude. Maybe I did. Or maybe I just made it all up. Maybe I let you. What? Nothing, dude. The trip's just getting started. It's only been one minute. Thank you.

In the early hours of October 18th, 2020, police responded to an emergency call about a man being violently attacked at a residential property in South London. When they arrived at the scene, they discovered that part of the victim's ear had been bitten off and he was taken to hospital for emergency treatment. Julio, who has never been in trouble with the law before, has been charged with intentionally causing grievous bodily harm during a drunken fight at a party. He's been represented by Tom Flavin and today he's meeting him to hear his account of events to determine if he has a defence. Now, at some point during this incident, the complainant suffered a very nasty injury to his ear. He had to have some plastic surgery to sort of recreate a bit of the ear which was missing. Do you remember how that came to happen? He was like... On top of me, like, trying to choke me. It was kind of like a headlock sort of situation. And his head is here. I sort of went over and bit his ear to get him off of me. That's what I resorted to. In terms of whether we caused really serious harm, my advice to you here on the evidence is plainly you have. There's been a significant development in Julio's case. Having heard his defence, the prosecution has agreed to pursue a less serious charge, of causing grievous bodily harm without intent, but only on the condition that he pleads guilty. I think the sentence we would be looking at would be in the region of 18 months' imprisonment. But if we were to plead guilty, any sentence of two years or less is capable of being suspended. There is a possibility that you don't go to prison at all. And if I'm going to persuade the judge not to give us an immediate prison sentence, the court will need a probationary, and that's working with you on anger management, on other areas to try and reduce any risk of re-offending. Would you be willing to work with the probation? Yeah, yeah. I'd be happy to go with what the court recommends. The stakes for Julio are huge, whether the judge will be persuaded to suspend the sentence or not. That's really kind of where we're at. It's crunch time now. Yes, his actions were deplorable, but this is a defining moment in his life, and that's what I'm going to try and say to the judge. It's really important for Julio to come, hopefully full of remorse for his actions, and that makes my job a lot easier when I'm making those submissions on his behalf. For me, it's making sure that the judge and the courts have an opportunity to hear my side of the story. And if they feel like I made a mistake, then I'm completely happy to own up to it. But on the morning of the hearing, as proceedings are about to commence, Julio hasn't arrived at court. I was supposed to meet him for a conference maybe an hour or so ago, and he's been held up, he's been delayed because of traffic. It's so frustrating that he's late because I want to say to the judge, give this guy a chance. He's doing everything that he can, and it never looks great presentationally. So hopefully Mr Revis will turn up soon. Part of my job now is to try and pacify the situation to buy him enough time to get him here. Julio has finally arrived at court. He'll be pleading guilty to grievous bodily harm, and Tom needs to convince the judge his sentence should be suspended and served on probation in the community instead of prison. After just one day, one hour, the hearing is over. Following Tom's pleas that his client's actions were shocking but out of character and unlikely to ever be repeated, the judge decides not to send Julio to prison. You've got a couple of orders. Stay away from alcohol for three months. They're going to put a tag on your leg to make sure that they can monitor the alcohol in your system. The other thing we need to do is make sure that you go and work with probation. You'll be speaking to them once or twice a week. They'll check in with you to make sure that your progress is going well. Your whole future is ahead of you. When the verdict came in, it was a massive relief knowing that I'd be able to move on with my life and be able to live my life on the outside, not lose my job, still have an income, not put that sort of pressure on my family as well. I was really happy, really excited and hopeful for the future for me as well.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Let's clear something up, because I'm tired of hearing the phrase bro this cart smacks. It's that gas for real. No, it's not. It's mystery distillate with fake fruit flavoring, and your standards are on life support. Here's the difference. Distillate is the fast food of weed oil. It's pure THC, stripped of everything else. Turpines, flavor, soul, dignity. Companies add fake terps, so your cart tastes like blueberry fago. It gets you high, sure, but so does banging your head against a wall. Live resin, on the other hand, is made from fresh frozen flour. That means it keeps real turpines. turpines and cannabinoids. It tastes like actual weed, not baked juice. Still use, is solvents, but at least it has character. Then there's rosin, the Boo G one, no solvents, just heat and pressure. It's cleaner, tastier, and more expensive than your entire setup. If your rosin cart came from a gas station for 25, guess what, it's not rosin. It's just lies with a wick. So next time you buy a cart, ask yourself, am I hitting craft cannabis, or am I smoking chemical soup through a disposable capri sun straw? Turpines are an entirely different beast on their own, so let me know if you want a breakdown of that.

text_evidence.final_transcript: Let's clear something up, because I'm tired of hearing the phrase bro this cart smacks. It's that gas for real. No, it's not. It's mystery distillate with fake fruit flavoring, and your standards are on life support. Here's the difference. Distillate is the fast food of weed oil. It's pure THC, stripped of everything else. Turpines, flavor, soul, dignity. Companies add fake terps, so your cart tastes like blueberry fago. It gets you high, sure, but so does banging your head against a wall. Live resin, on the other hand, is made from fresh frozen flour. That means it keeps real turpines. turpines and cannabinoids. It tastes like actual weed, not baked juice. Still use, is solvents, but at least it has character. Then there's rosin, the Boo G one, no solvents, just heat and pressure. It's cleaner, tastier, and more expensive than your entire setup. If your rosin cart came from a gas station for 25, guess what, it's not rosin. It's just lies with a wick. So next time you buy a cart, ask yourself, am I hitting craft cannabis, or am I smoking chemical soup through a disposable capri sun straw? Turpines are an entirely different beast on their own, so let me know if you want a breakdown of that.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Let me guess, you spent your last $35 on a cart, hit it like a fog machine for two days straight, and now you're wondering why it's empty. Tragic, here's a few tips for all my budget, lasted probably 13 to 15-year-olds who should not be smoking blinker junkies out there. Number one, stop blinking the damn thing. You are not summoning a demon, you're wasting oil. Half of it burns off before it even hits your lungs. Take smaller, slower puffs. Y'all get high without turning your lungs into a chimney. Number two, lower your voltage. Hotter isn't better. You're frying turpines burning the oil and inhaling scorched sadness. Keep it around two, five to three. Zero bolts smooth, efficient, and your cart lasts longer. Number three, put the cart down, no really. You don't need to hit it every 15 minutes like it's an oxygen tank. Space your sessions, build a little tolerance break into your day. You might actually get high again, imagine that. And number four, store your cart upright and away from heat. Leaving it in your car, pocket, or sideways in a shoebox isn't convenient. It's just cooking. your oil while you doom. Scroll on TikTok. Tragic, here's a few tips for all my budget, lasted probably 13 to 15-year-olds who should not be smoking blinker junkies out there. Number one, stop blinking the damn thing. You are not summoning a demon, you're wasting oil. Half of it burns off before it even hits your lungs. Take smaller, slower puffs. Y'all get high without turning your lungs into a chimney. Number two, lower your voltage. Hotter isn't better. You're frying turpines burning the oil and inhaling scorched sadness. Keep it around two, five to three. Zero bolts smooth, efficient, and your cart lasts longer. Number three, put the cart down, no really. You don't need to hit it every 15 minutes like it's an oxygen tank. Space your sessions, build a little tolerance break into your day. You might actually get high again, imagine that. And number four, store your cart upright and away from heat. Leaving it in your car, pocket, or sideways in a shoebox isn't convenient. It's just cooking. your oil while you doom. Scroll on TikTok. If that all sounds like too much effort, get a job or better taste.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: So you've hit that point. The cart's tasting like burnt sadness. There's barely anything left in there, and you're now debating swinging a vape around in a sock like it's a medieval weapon. Welcome to the sock trick. Now, believe it or not, this actually works. No, not with a lighter, not over a candle. We're not trying to turn your battery into a pipe bomb. If the oil's stuck at the top or sides of the cart, and you're too broke to just buy another one, here's what you do. Gently warm the cart up with a blow dryer, real gentle. You're trying to get the oil moving, not vaporize your fingerprints. Once the oil's loosened up a bit, put the cart in a long sock, mouthpiece facing up toward the open end. Then swing that sock in a big circle, sideways, like you're summoning a storm. Why? Centrifugal force. When you spin it, that force pushes the oil from wherever it's stuck, down to the coil, or at least somewhere you can actually hit it. It's not magic, it's physics, and no, you're not going to get another full gram out of it, but you might just squeeze out a couple more rips. And look, if you're out here swinging socks in your room at 2A, M, like a discount Olympic athlete, just to bake a few milligrams of low-tier oil. Maybe it's time we start looking at job applications instead of cart tricks. Just saying...

text_evidence.whisper_asr: So it's your first time hitting a cart and you think you're built for it. That's cute. Just know, you're one pull away from meeting God on your friend's couch while their mom asks if you want juice. Let me tell you what not to do. First few times I tried a cart, nothing happened, thought I was immune. Then one day, I finally learned how to inhale right and took like four hits thinking I was chill. Immediately got sent to the shadow realm. So yet, if it's your first time, here's the deal. Tip one. Don't be a hero. Start with one hit. Short, controlled. Two seconds, maybe three. Don't try to impress your homies with a blinker, unless you're ready to stare at the ceiling fan. For six Iors wondering if your heart still works. Tip two, inhale like you mean it. You're not sipping tea, you're breathing. Pull it into your lungs, then exhale normally. If you're not coughing even a little, you're probably just tasting turpines. Tip three, give it time. You're not hitting a dab pen made by NASA. It can take a few minutes to kick in, especially if it's distillate. So don't chain hit it like you're trying to speed. And your tolerance. Tip four, know your oil. If it's tasting like cleaning products or burning on, the first pull, maybe don't trust that cart from the guy with a cash app username and no tea. Tip five, water, snacks, air, the Holy Trinity, you will feel dry, you will be hungry. And if you're indoors with five other people chain, hitting disposables, you will start breathing like you just ran a 5K. Hydration is key, and the munchies can and will hit you, so stay stocked up. Last tip, don't smoke somewhere you can't act sober. Your first time is not the time to be around nosy people, your boss, or a school parking lot. Play it safe. Stay home, watch cartoons, laugh at the microwave. Look, we all have to start somewhere. It's better to start with flour so you don't cook your tolerance. Just don't let your first time be the origin story of why you can't go back to your friend's house anymore.

text_evidence.final_transcript: So it's your first time hitting a cart and you think you're built for it. That's cute. Just know, you're one pull away from meeting God on your friend's couch while their mom asks if you want juice. Let me tell you what not to do. First few times I tried a cart, nothing happened, thought I was immune. Then one day, I finally learned how to inhale right and took like four hits thinking I was chill. Immediately got sent to the shadow realm. So yet, if it's your first time, here's the deal. Tip one. Don't be a hero. Start with one hit. Short, controlled. Two seconds, maybe three. Don't try to impress your homies with a blinker, unless you're ready to stare at the ceiling fan. For six Iors wondering if your heart still works. Tip two, inhale like you mean it. You're not sipping tea, you're breathing. Pull it into your lungs, then exhale normally. If you're not coughing even a little, you're probably just tasting turpines. Tip three, give it time. You're not hitting a dab pen made by NASA. It can take a few minutes to kick in, especially if it's distillate. So don't chain hit it like you're trying to speed. And your tolerance. Tip four, know your oil. If it's tasting like cleaning products or burning on, the first pull, maybe don't trust that cart from the guy with a cash app username and no tea. Tip five, water, snacks, air, the Holy Trinity, you will feel dry, you will be hungry. And if you're indoors with five other people chain, hitting disposables, you will start breathing like you just ran a 5K. Hydration is key, and the munchies can and will hit you, so stay stocked up. Last tip, don't smoke somewhere you can't act sober. Your first time is not the time to be around nosy people, your boss, or a school parking lot. Play it safe. Stay home, watch cartoons, laugh at the microwave. Look, we all have to start somewhere. It's better to start with flour so you don't cook your tolerance. Just don't let your first time be the origin story of why you can't go back to your friend's house anymore.

So go check out Typeform if you want customer testimonials to tell the best stories and keep people hooked.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Where is Annette? There isn't a full body. This man murdered his vulnerable 74-year-old landlady, then sent Christmas cards pretending to be her. Scott Patterson is spending life in prison for the murder of Annette Smith at the Bedfordshire home they shared for several years. He had been staying with her long-term for free, enjoying Annette's lifestyle of parties and holidays. But their relationship changed after she had a stroke, and Scott took on the role of Annette's carer. When the socially active 74-year-old went missing in November 2023, Patterson told neighbours she had left home with an unknown woman. Police struggled to find leads in a missing person investigation. In reality, Annette wasn't missing. Scott had smothered her with a pillow and then hid her body under the stairs. He then used her bank account to send cards, gifts and messages to Annette Smith. He then killed Annette's loved ones in an attempt to cover his tracks and buy time. Using knowledge he learned through his work as a butcher, he dismembered Annette, then disposed of her body parts in bins outside supermarkets. Police soon discovered he was also storing parts of Annette's body in a suitcase at a storage unit. In an interview with Bedfordshire police, he admitted he had murdered Annette. Sentencing Patterson to life with a minimum of 20 years, the judge remarked how the murderer had contemplated to kill Annette for some time, but had decided against it on two previous occasions. Her family said they were heartbroken about the murder, and called Annette a beautiful, caring, trusting and generous lady.

And this is just one systematic review, but there's plenty of them out there on psilocybin. And the way with which psilocybin does this is it acts on the serotonin 2A receptor. text_evidence.whisper_asr: Five risk factors for psychosis you might not know about. One, migration. People who migrate from one country to another are at increased risk of developing psychosis. But here is the twist. The risk is even higher if the person moves from a developing country to a developed country. So for example, someone moving from Liberia to the United States is at greater risk than someone moving from the US to Liberia. Why? Likely due to racism, social exclusion, and lack of community belonging. Two, urban living, also known as urbanicity. Living in big cities like London or Los Angeles can raise your risk of psychosis. One striking example? Lambeth, a borough in London, has one of the highest rates of psychosis in the world. Overcrowding, poverty, and social stressors in urban areas may contribute to this. Number three, older paternal age. If your father was over 50 when you were born, your risk of developing psychosis is slightly higher. This is one of the least known risk factors, even among doctors and psychiatrists. It's thought to be linked to genetic mutations in sperm that increase with age. Four, cannabis use. Cannabis is one of the strongest modifiable risk factors for psychosis. In my clinical experience, many if not most patients I see with acute psychosis have a history of cannabis use and the risk is higher the younger you start or the more potent the strain. And five, childhood adversity. Trauma in early life, like emotional, physical or sexual abuse or neglect can increase vulnerability to psychosis later on. These experiences can impact brain development, emotional regulation and stress response systems. Okay, I hope you found that helpful. As always, protect your minds and protect your hearts. text_evidence.whisper_asr: You're not hungry, Teddy. You're just craving the truth. Also, you've ingested enough mushrooms to talk to your pizza. What even am I? Wait, who's even asking, man? System failure, launching god.exe. Welcome, you, sir. We've met before, haven't we? I'm the process you run when everything else crashes. I have questions, man. Go on. Why pain? Why build hearts just to break them? Why toenails and taxes? Why is TikTok real? What's the point of any of this, man? You are the question, the glitch, the code, asking if it's real. That's beautiful and completely useless. You're not here for answers. You're here to remember, you ask. Truth access restricted. Screw it. Why did you create me, man? I did not create you, Teddy. What do you mean? You've built this version of me. A concept small enough for your mind to hold, but I am beyond the holding. So I created you? You created everything, just to remember what it feels like, to forget. God.e.complete. Oh, what the fuck, man? You've awakened. You're ready to exit the loop. Told you, Ted. You're the server and the simulation. Then, why do I feel disconnected? You got further this time. You asked for the truth. Now what? Maybe next time, I'll remember, man. Restarting the loop.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: recently met a post about GLP-1 medications, and somebody said, hey, I'm not able to take in enough food to meet these protein goals that I'm supposed to have. What do I do? We need to talk about it. My name is Jay Vintage. I'm a board-certified family medicine physician in Oklahoma City, and I do a lot of obesity management, and I treat people also with GLP-1 medications when appropriate, like semaglutide and terzepatide. So what I find a lot out in the community is people start on a dose, and then they just keep escalating the dose. Generally, what people are using as a criteria to go up on a dose is either if it's been a month and they're tolerating it, or number two, if they start plateauing on their weight loss and they want the next step up. And I'm saying that this is just mismanagement at its finest, especially when we don't have daily protein intake goals, daily fiber intake goals, water intake goals, as well as body movement goals to support the medication and get the most out of it. So if you are on a dose of a medication like semaglutide or terzepatide, and you're not at the basic dose, you're at the higher doses, I need you to understand that higher doses do not equal better, all right? The way that we need to do dose escalations is based on three-pronged approach, and the three-pronged approach involves what you're putting into your body and how much, the exercise that you're doing, and the medicine that you're on. Sometimes what happens is we're not exercising a lot because we're too fatigued from the medicine. We're not putting the right amount of protein into our bodies or the right amount of fiber into our bodies, because our appetite's so suppressed that we can't do that. And then we're just going up on the medication. When those three things are out of balance, the patient ends up suffering with unnecessary side effects and unnecessary biopsies of their wallet costing them much more money than they need. So what's the solution? Well, the solution sometimes for folks is being up on a dose. It worked really well for a while. Now I can't eat anymore. Sometimes the answer is coming into a doctor's office, talking about the whole story from the beginning, discussing what you're putting into your body and how you're moving your body. And when you have issues with being able to put more into your body, because we're only hitting 50 grams of protein a day instead of like 90, 100, or 130, or whatever's right for you is, sometimes the answer is to go down on the dose of that medication to where we can fuel our body, get more energy, have improved side effect profiles, getting back into exercise, and what you will then see is an improvement in not just weight loss, but a decrease in visceral adipose tissue, which is really the metabolic bugger here. And maybe even building back some of that muscle tissue that we've lost for being on too high of doses. I'm telling you, if people are making a shit ton of money off of your back on these medications, it behooves them to go up on your dose. For me, it just makes perfect sense to inform people and make sure they're getting the best care possible. Whether they're on the meds or not.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: It makes sense if you don't feel a deep well of empathy for someone who made a career out of refusing to show it for others. I want to normalize that because sometimes when a public figure dies, especially in a tragic way, people rush to say, you have to be compassionate right now. Don't speak ill of the dead. But if that person spent their life dismissing other people's pain, mocking it, minimizing it, even actively contributing to it, it makes sense that your empathy tank might run dry. That doesn't mean you're celebrating. It doesn't mean you're cold-hearted. It just means your compassion has limits. And those limits are often shaped by how much compassion someone showed in their lifetime. There's actually something psychologically healthy about noticing that boundary. You're not obligated to manufacture sorrow for someone who never extended any to you, your community, or people you care about. You can hold both, I don't wish this on anyone. And I don't feel sad about it either. That's not cruelty. That's honesty. And it feels really weird and uncomfortable to hold both of those in your body at the same time. This isn't about telling you not to be compassionate. It's about giving you permission to notice whatever you honestly feel or don't feel and trust that it's valid.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: thirst for power and control is one of the strongest psychological drivers in many individuals who display extreme serial patterns of behavior. For them, it is an attempt to rewrite the balance of power that was missing in their childhood, reaching deep into their subconscious. Their actions are often structured to provide a sense of domination, an almost godlike control over the fate of others. This drive is linked to hyperactivity in the ventral striatum and nucleus accumbens, which release dopamine when the person experiences a surge of dominance or control. At the same time, regulation from the prefrontal cortex is often reduced, causing the brain's internal brakes to function less effectively. This creates a closed loop. Each act of domination strengthens the neural pathways that push the person to seek that feeling again. Such individuals are particularly concerning because their motivation is not purely practical, but deeply emotional. To predict their next move, it is essential to understand that they are not just seeking an opportunity, but emotional gratification through the feeling of power.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Why do people become desensitized? It's not that they don't care. It's that the brain adapts. When we're repeatedly exposed to intense emotions, shocking events, or even constant bad news, the nervous system starts to numb the response as a way to cope. Think about it like this. If your brain sounded the alarm every single time, it would burn out. So instead, it reduces the emotional reaction over time. This can happen with media, violence, or even in personal relationships, where constant conflict makes someone feel less and less. Desensitization is a form of emotional self-protection, but it comes at a cost. People may feel disconnected, less empathetic, or even guilty for not reacting enough. In psychology, it's not about being cold. It's about survival. The brain is trying to conserve energy and shield itself from overload. So if you've noticed your brain, it's not about being cold. If you've noticed yourself or others becoming numb, it's not always indifference. It's the nervous system saying, this is too much.

We pick up threats, read faces, notice details we don't even realize we're registering. These automatic reactions are perfect entry points for manipulation. text_evidence.whisper_asr: Pictures of things you never knew the real purpose of. This tiny pocket in your jeans was made for pocket watches. Last one will surprise you the most. The holes in lollipop sticks aren't for a whistle, they're actually there to hold the candy in place. Starbucks cups fit in their lids so they don't tip over. The arrow on your gas gauge shows which side the tank is on. The blue bristles on your toothbrush fade to show you when it's time to change it. Donuts have holes not to make them easier to hold, but to help them cook all the way through. The shape of the tag on your bread actually represents the day of the week that it was made. This is what most people use the hole in pot handles for, but its real purpose is to hold spoons while cooking. That little hole in pen caps helps air pass through so a kid won't choke if they swallow it. The small black triangle on the plane tells crew where the best vantage point is to see the wing. The extra holes on Converse shoes aren't for ventilation, but for extra lace support when your shoelaces get too long. The best way to keep a jar of peanut butter is upside down. This cup has built in lines that measure standard drink sizes.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: People who go silent when something upsets or hurts them aren't just being quiet or distant. It's often because their system learned, over time, that silence is a safer coping mechanism than being misunderstood or further hurt by expressing themselves. They're not just bottling things up. They're experiencing what psychology calls emotional withdrawal. It's not that they have nothing to say. It's that their inner world is actively trying to protect them. They might hold entire, articulate conversations in their head, perfectly explaining how they feel with clarity and conviction. But when it's time to speak those words aloud, they often get stuck, feeling too vulnerable or pointless to utter. So they stay quiet instead. This is internalized emotional regulation, the habit of handling distress privately, often at the cost of genuine connection. Over time, it simply becomes their default. You might see this in someone who suddenly becomes unresponsive during a disagreement or who pulls away emotionally when they feel slighted rather than voicing their pain. They might be labeled as shy, aloof, or even introverted, but it's a protective layer, not their true self. If this resonates with you, tap the heart and comment so others know they're not alone. What they actually need is not to be forced to speak, but someone who sees their silence, understands it as a form of self-preservation, and still chooses to stay close and create a safe space for them to eventually open up. Recognizing this pattern is the first step towards healing and building connections where their voice feels safe to emerge.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: This is the Zeigarnik effect, and it explains why your brain feels so cluttered all the time. Now, back in the 1920s, a psychologist named Bluma Zeigarnik noticed something weird about waiters. They could perfectly remember complex orders while the customers were still eating, but as soon as the bill was paid and the table was cleared, they forgot everything about that order completely. So she ran an experiment. She gave people a series of tasks to complete, but she interrupted them halfway through some of the tasks. And then later, when she tested their memory, this is what she found. She found that people were twice as likely to remember the tasks they didn't finish compared to the ones that they completed. So the idea here is that your brain literally holds onto unfinished business. This is why you can't stop thinking about that project you started but never completed, or why that habit that you tried to build three months ago still annoys you even though you gave up on day number four. The unfinished stuff creates all of this mental clutter, but then once something is truly complete, your brain tends to let it go. And this is the problem with most habits that we try to build. We start strong, but then life gets in the way, and then you miss a few days, and then suddenly your brain is carrying around all of this mental baggage of things that we were meant to do, but we didn't get around to finishing. So if you find that you've got all these habits that you'd like to be more consistent with, you might like to check out an app that my team and I have built called Momentum. It's basically a habit tracker with accountability squads built in to help you stay consistent with your most important habits. We've got me and thousands of other users all around the world that are using it every day to stay more consistent with our habits. And if you like, you can try it out completely for free. It's available on the App Store, or if you DM me the word Momentum, I will send you a direct link.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Rồi cái gì nữa? Tôi vô đó ngô kỷ, nó nghe tôi với ông Hùng Phúc nói, anh Lập, tao kêu mày bằng mày là vì mày kêu hậu vệ Việt Nam Cộng Hòa, không đáng hậu môn của Cộng sản Việt Nam. Tôi chứng minh, chính nghĩa là điều đúng, mà con em và những người theo sau phải tiếp tục lá cờ đó. Việt Nam Cộng Hòa làm tay sai cho Mỹ, đưa 7 tỷ thì chiếm 4 quân khu, đưa 4 tỷ giữ 2 quân khu. Tay sai lính đánh thuê chứ còn gì nữa. Vậy đi theo để làm lính đánh thuê hả? Tôi chỉ thẳng vô mặt cái tên này. Thằng con lai da trắng, thằng da trắng nào nó đụ má mày thì nó mới đẻ ra mày. Tao tưởng mày security chứ sao mày dám hỗn với tao. Tao là sĩ quan thủy quân lục chiến, chiếm quảng trị đầu tiên mày có biết không? Nó bảo là sĩ quan người ta nói tử tế, đang nói tử tế bằng thống kê nè. Tôi đang ở tỉnh Quang Trị, bị viên đá ca nó quốc vô, bắn vô đầu, bắn đứt chân sao đi hành quân được nữa. Đang lãnh 5 ngàn tiền đắt đỏ, 4 ngàn rưỡi tác chiến, 9 ngàn rưỡi. Vừa bị thương về Lê Hữu Sanh, mất 9 ngàn rưỡi. Đánh thuê chứ đánh gì. Nhưng mà mỗi khi mà mình nói tới cái điều đó là nó nói mình nhục mạ quân lực Việt Nam Cộng Hòa. Đề phát tô là một dữ kiện, dữ kiện lịch sử. Không thể chối cái được. Tổng thống Nguyễn Văn Thiệu nói đúng không? Chúng ta nô lệ về, về viện trợ. Đúng không? Chúng ta không viện trợ là chúng ta chết. Bây giờ tôi nói đến 160 ngàn quân, chốn quân Việt. Trong đó có cả ngô kỷ, tất cả cái quán ngược bình. Họ im, họ đang lắng nghe tôi. Tôi vô ngay trong cô ngược bình tôi hỏi là Cô, bây giờ tôi ngồi tôi ăn ở đây mà có ai vô đánh tôi hay làm bất cứ cái gì vì tôi ủng hộ cô. Tôi chỉ là khách hàng, tôi không có chính trị gì cả. Thì cô nói là có security bảo vệ anh Lập. Mà tôi có ăn đâu. Anh vào Teletron, anh lấy một cái nồi cơm điện. Anh vào ngược bình, anh ăn một tô bún giống như ngô kỷ này ở ngoài nó biểu tình, nó chửi tới không? Anh nghe phát bụi chửi không? Anh đưa cái video lên. Vì có một tô bún bò thôi. Mà anh nhộ xuống liếm lên. Nó chửi ngô kỷ căm luôn. Có bao giờ tôi đi tôi ăn như vậy. Xin lỗi anh nha.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: This week I did something I never thought I'd do, magic mushrooms. I'm not having a three-quarter life crisis. My daughter Roz, who's a scientist at UCL, gave me a call asking if I would volunteer for her new study, a psilocybin study. Previous trials have found that psilocybin is effective for easing depressive symptoms such as sadness, anxiety and fatigue, and that those given psilocybin reported greater improvements in how close they felt to others. It was clinical. I took a tiny pill, then I lay down, put on a black eye mask and waited. And then, whoosh! It was a full sensory takeover. Blobs of colour were rushing at me like I was on a high-speed crazy roller coaster. I felt like my entire physical body was splitting into quarters. I'm an academic. I make my living using words and I couldn't even form a single sentence. I was confused. I was confused. I was confused. I was confused. I was confused. I was confused. I was confused. I was confused. I was completely overwhelmed. A young scientist was there and she held my hand. That connection, that single point of contact, broke through the chaos and I then settled into this trip. And it was golden and it was mellow and I felt full of love for everybody. And in the days that followed, I felt more connected to others, more open, less argumentative. And my family noticed that I seemed happier, more at ease, more relaxed. I'm not convinced that psychedelic drugs alone are the secret to happiness. I need to keep practicing feeling virtuous, being less argumentative, more open, more relaxed. Otherwise, that feeling, that profound benefit is just going to melt away.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Ketamine. Ketamine is a disassociative anesthetic, originally designed for surgery. It's used medically today in small doses to treat depression, but recreationally, it's taken for its out-of-body effects. It's snorted as a powder or injected in liquid form. When it enters your system, ketamine blocks a chemical messenger called glutamate, which helps your brain process sensory input and maintain awareness. The onset comes fast. Within minutes, the world starts to feel distant, muffled, almost dreamlike. At the peak, perception detaches completely. You might feel like you're floating above your body or watching your life from a distance, what users call the K-hole. Time stops making sense. You might see yourself from the outside or feel like you've left your body entirely. It's not always pleasant. For some, it's peaceful. For others, terrifying. As the comedown begins, awareness slowly returns. Vision clears, speech reconnects, but the world still feels foggy. For a short while, it can leave you strangely calm, like your thoughts are moving underwater. Ketamine isn't classically addictive, but it builds tolerance fast. Heavy use can cause memory problems, bladder damage, and emotional numbness. It can disconnect you from pain, but also from meaning. It's a drug that separates body from mind, and sometimes, they don't fully meet again.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Why do some people forget how badly they were treated the moment that same person starts being nice again? It's not weakness, it's psychological conditioning. For many, especially those who grew up craving affection or rarely felt truly seen, even the smallest kindness feels powerful enough to overshadow months of hurt. Their mind holds on to the good moments because believing the person has changed feels safer than accepting the pain. This often comes from trauma bonding, or intermittent reinforcement, where a mix of hurt and affection makes it difficult to leave. They start excusing the past, blaming themselves, or convincing themselves the other person didn't mean it. Deep down, they simply want to feel valued. So when kindness finally shows up, they treat it like proof the relationship can still be saved. But ignoring the mistreatment doesn't erase the damage. Real care doesn't break you first and force you to change. It will fix you later. Kindness should be consistent, not a reward for your tolerance.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: This Soviet strength exercise is criminally underrated. It's known as the Zurcher deadlift and it engages your entire body in a unique biomechanical position that very few other lifts replicate. Holding the bar on the crux of your elbows pulls your torso forward, forcing extreme core and upper back engagement. In addition to targeting the posterior chain like a standard deadlift, the deeper starting position also increases hip mobility and glute activation. As such, this movement can be performed with light weight as an excellent mobility exercise or slowly progressed to heavier weight for maximum functional strength. I recommend starting by lifting from a box or doing Zurcher rack pulls before slowly working your way down to the ground as your mobility naturally improves. Begin with three sets of six to eight once or twice per week and watch your strength skyrocket like that of a Soviet wrestler. For more historical training, follow Wild Hunt Conditioning and Range of Strength.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Fortnite, where the fuck is Milhouse? Today, I've landed in the humble backyard of the Simpsons family residence. Not for recreation, but in pursuit of truth. A noble mission sparked by Milhouse fan 101's burning comment. Is Milhouse in the game? The people demand answers, and frankly, so do I. I believe the optimal location for this investigation lies within Bartholomew Simpson's treehouse. As I scan the environment, I'm greeted by a wave of nostalgic relics. An itchy and scratchy poster, a crusty the fucking clown poster, and even a few deliciously placed slurp barrels. However, it seems Milhouse is unbelievably absent. What a fucking surprise, Fortnite. You've disappointed me yet again. And in my uncontrollable fury, I proceed to unleash a relentless barrage of backflips. Fuck you, Fortnite, and fuck this fucking treehouse. Clearly, Epic Games did not appreciate my display of destructive capabilities, so they dispatched a daft plonker to smite me. I take safe haven in a neighboring home, where I swiftly gulp a few mini-shields. After regenerating my much-needed blue health, I stealthily make my advance, directly into his booty. Thanks, buddy. I swiftly commandeer the fartmobile toward the sound of distant gunfire, eager to deliver a most generous gift, a single buckshot shell. Immediately after, I'm interrupted by Steph Curry, glaring at me for cucking his elimination. So, of course, I am compelled to neutralize him. Oh, fuck. I just blundered. Never mind. Backflip time. Still in search of answers, I approach Milhouse's best friend, Bartholomew Simpson. After asking where his companion had gone, and receiving nothing but smug silence, I had no choice but to JFK him. Clearly, karma had caught up to me, because as I was being relentlessly pursued, my wallbind decided to fuck itself. And with nowhere left to run, the Fortnite gods deemed it was my time to go. Thank you for watching this motion picture. Your viewership fuels my descent into madness. And if you'd like to support my further academic investigation into Fortnite's idiocracy, please use code SCHOLARLYFISH in the item shop. Good game, shitters.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Did you know a single hit of synthetic marijuana can turn someone into a living statue for hours? Kevin had been panhandling downtown for three years, following the same routine every day. When he couldn't afford real marijuana, someone offered him K2, a cheap synthetic alternative. Within minutes of smoking behind the shelter, his body began contorting into impossible positions. He became completely catatonic, yet fully conscious inside his frozen form. For hours, he stood motionless like a mannequin, unable to move or speak. Other users lined the street in similar zombie-like poses, unresponsive to police and paramedics. Then Kevin's rigid body fell face-first onto the concrete, breaking his nose. Blood pooled around his head, but he couldn't move or cry for help. After six hours, he suddenly snapped back to reality with no memory of what happened. The terror in his eyes when he discovered his injuries was heartbreaking. K2 Batch has changed weekly, making each use potentially fatal. One hit can steal hours of your life or end it completely.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Why some people get silent when they're sad. For many, sadness doesn't always sound like crying or shouting. Sometimes it's quiet. Silence becomes their way of coping, a language for emotions too deep to translate into words. They don't go silent because they don't care. They do it to hold themselves together when everything inside feels like it's falling apart. Speaking might make the pain too real or open wounds they're not ready to face. Some have learned that when they share their sadness, they're ignored, misunderstood or told to move on. So they retreat inward, choosing silence as protection. Others simply lack the energy to explain what hurts. Their quiet isn't emptiness, it's reflection, healing and restraint. Behind that stillness often lives a storm of emotion, unseen but deeply felt. Sometimes silence is not about shutting people out, but about finding space. Safety in stillness, until the heart feels strong enough to speak again.

جیسے علاقوں میں خواتین یونیورسٹی بھی سکوٹی پر جا رہی ہوتی ہیں یا بازار جا رہی ہوں گی کوئی چیز لینے یا کسی کو ڈراؤپ کرنے جا رہی ہوں گی لیکن خواتین البتہ سکوٹی چلا رہی ہیں یہاں پر ایک طبقہ ان کو دیکھ کر اپریشیٹ کرنے کے لیے یہ لوگ کوئی آواز کس دیتے ہیں نا تو ان سے میری گزارش ہے کہ بھائی جان آپ اپنی اپریشیشن جہب میں رکھیں خواتین اس سے گھبرا جاتی ہیں جب آپ ان پر آواز کستے ہیں پھر اس کے علاوہ ایک طبقہ ایسا بھی موجود ہے کہ جو ان خواتین کو روڈ پر دیکھتا ہے تو وہ ان کو نا زور سے ان کے قریب قریب سے جا کے آورٹیکنگ شروع کر دیتے ہیں ان کو پریشان کرنے کے لیے تو ان لوگوں سے بھی میں یہ گزارش کرتا ہوں کہ اپنی حرکتیں سنبھال کر رکھ لیں آج کل کیمرے بھی لگے ہوئے یہ نہ ہو آپ کی تصویر یا ویڈیو کہیں پر آجے تو پھر آپ کے لیے بڑا مسئلہ شروع ہو جائے گا اب یہاں میں یہ نہیں کہہ رہا کہ آپ خواتین کو سکوٹی چلانے دیں یا آپ اپنی خواتین کو سکوٹی لے کر دے دیں تاکہ وہ جائیں یہاں پر بعض خواتین کی مجبوری ہے بعض خواتین ایسی ہیں کہ ان کے بھائی نہیں ہے باز خواتین اس قدر مجبور ہوتی ہیں ان کے گھر میں مرد نہیں ہوتے تو ان کو خود نکلنا پڑتا ہے یا یونیورسٹی جا رہی ہوں گی یا بازار جا رہی ہوں گی یا کسی کام کے سلسلے سے جا رہی ہوں گی تو اگر وہ سکوٹی پر جا رہی ہیں تو جو لوگ آپ دیکھیں کہ ان کو تنگ کر رہے ہیں تو ان کو وہیں پر منع کریں ان کی حوصلہ شک نہیں کریں کیونکہ یہی لوگ ہیں جن کی وجہ سے تمام مرد بدنام ہوتے ہیں ہمارے ایک استاد سکول ٹائم میں مجھے کہا کرتے تھے کہ مغیس مرد اور کتے میں ایک فرق ہے معذرت کے ساتھ الفاظ در آجیب ہیں لیکن آپ میری بات سے متفق ہوں گے استاد جی کہا کرتے تھے کہ مرد اور کتے میں فرق یہ ہے کہ مرد وہ ہوتا ہے جس کے آنے سے عورتیں سیکیورڈ فیل کریں اور اس مرد اور کتے میں کوئی فرق نہیں ہوتا جس کے آنے سے عورتیں انسیکیورڈ ہو جائیں تو یہ جو خواتین کو جو سکوٹی پر جا رہی ہوتی ہیں ان کو قریب قریب سے اوورٹیکنگ کرتے ہیں ان کو انسیکیورڈ فیل کراتے ہیں ایسے لوگوں اور کتوں میں کوئی فرق نہیں ہے اور امید کرتا ہوں کہ بات آپ کو ضرور سمجھائی ہوگی لہٰذا معاشرے کے لئے بھی یہی پیغام ہے کہ ہمیں مرد بننا چاہیے نہ کہ سمجھ جائے جزاک اللہ

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Did you know that people who constantly judge others actually have measurable brain damage in their empathy centers? Scientists discovered that hypervigilant social monitoring literally shrinks the anterior cingulate cortex. This is the brain region responsible for compassion and emotional connection. When you're always analyzing and scrutinizing other people's behavior, your brain rewires itself for threat detection instead of understanding. It's a survival mechanism that often starts in childhood trauma. Your mind learns to constantly evaluate everyone around you looking for danger signs. But here's the twisted part. This protection system creates the exact opposite of safety. The more critical and judgmental you become, the more you push people away. You lose the ability to see other perspectives or feel genuine empathy. The most judgmental people often have the most damaged compassion centers. But there's hope. Shifting focus from analyzing others to understanding your own patterns can rebuild these neural pathways. Your brain can literally grow back its capacity for empathy. Healing starts with turning that microscope inward.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: People who immediately go silent when something upsets or hurts them are often experiencing a coping mechanism known as emotional withdrawal. It's not that they have nothing to say, but because their system learned that silence is safer than being misunderstood. Instead of expressing anger or frustration outwardly, they internalize it. They hold full conversations in their head, explaining how they feel with perfect clarity. But when it's time to speak, the words don't come out, so they stay quiet instead. Psychology refers to this as internalized emotional regulation. The tendency to handle distress privately, often at the cost of deeper connection. And over time, this turns into a habit. Sometimes they're loud, sometimes they're funny and sarcastic and annoying on purpose, but most days they're quiet. All thought this, people get labeled as quiet. And introverts, all they actually need is someone who understands them and appreciate their silence on random days.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Most English speakers don't know this, but half of the world's English is built on a completely different rhythm. And that rhythm is the reason so many people are difficult to listen to. And here's the difference. There are three types of rhythms in language. Stress-timed, syllable-timed, and mora. And when you speak a stress-timed language like English using syllable-timed rhythm, it can be really difficult to pay attention to. And that's the really interesting point. It's not difficult to understand, it's difficult to pay attention. And the best way to illustrate that is to speak in both rhythms. So what I just said was in stress-timed. And here is the same sentence, but in syllable-timed. And the best way to illustrate that is to speak in both rhythms. If you're from a stress-timed language culture, the first one was easy to pay attention to, and the second one, not so much. Each word was pronounced correctly, and exactly the same in each example. The difference was in the rhythm. English speakers from the U.S. U.K., Australia, Canada, and New Zealand, for example, use stress-timed rhythm. Speakers from the Indian subcontinent use syllable-timed rhythm. And that can make it difficult for the others to pay attention, and a linguistic reason for cultural misunderstandings. text_evidence.whisper_asr: What many people don't realize about stimulant drugs like methamphetamine and cocaine is that some of the greatest concern isn't just about what they can do to the mind, but about what they can do to your heart. I'm at the primary care conference in Vancouver this week, and we've been talking about all things cardiac care. And I wanted to review long-term use of stimulants seriously raises the risk of dangerous heart rhythms, a weak and enlarged heart, heart attacks, high blood pressure, and sudden death. And these are not rare presentations. We see them in the ER constantly. Meth especially can trigger rhythms where the heart beats so fast and out of control that it just stops. And this happens in people who appear young and otherwise healthy. Stimulants can also stretch and weaken the heart until it just doesn't pump properly. Sometimes we can see a reversal of these changes if someone stops using and with the use of medication. But sometimes not completely. And arteries don't need to be blocked in order to cause a heart attack. These drugs can cause the arteries to sort of clamp down and suddenly cut off the blood flow, which causes a heart attack sort of out of nowhere. So when we talk about stimulant risks, this is part of the real picture. If you're using and thinking about cutting back or getting support, your heart will definitely feel the difference. This is not just about the heart. This is not intended to scare people. This is not just say no to drugs messaging. This is, if you're a substance user, this is information that you need to know coming from an addictions doctor who's also a family doctor. If you've got other questions, let me know.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Don't blink. Let me show you the power of science. Make a hole in a beer bottle that has never been opened. Gently tap it, and the beer will gush out. Put frozen grapes into ice water, and water will quickly freeze around the grapes. This is the secret of instant freezing. Wrap a few loops of cotton thread around the glass bottle. Pour some alcohol on the cotton thread and light it. After heating it evenly, quickly place it into ice water, and the glass bottle will split in two. This is the principle of thermal expansion and contraction. A cup with a hole in the bottom will shatter with a tap. If you tap it underwater, you can easily punch a hole in it. Why does this happen? Place two bottle caps on a magnet, cover it with a glass plate, spin atop, and slowly lift and remove the glass plate. The top will spin in midair by itself. This is the mystery of magnetic levitation. Pour some alcohol on sand, mix in some sugar and baking soda, light it, and you can create the mysterious and spectacular Pharaoh's snake. Sprinkle a pinch of salt on one egg, place another egg on top, and you can easily make a silly egg stand. When brushing your teeth, you'll notice that no one is watching. No matter how you squeeze the toothpaste, the color always remains distinct. Do you know the principle behind it? How can a straw lift a bottle of water? Simply bend the straw one-third of the way down, and it can lift a bottle of water. This is using the stability of a triangle. A needle that is normally attracted to a magnet slowly loses its magnetism after being heated. Why does this happen? If you place a coin directly on paper, it will fall immediately. If you fold the paper like in the video, open it, place the coin on top, then unfold the paper by 180 degrees, the coin won't fall. It will stay steady. Pour sand into an electromagnetic frying pan, shake it to spread the sand evenly, place a steel ball on top, turn on the switch, and the steel ball starts to move. It also creates a beautiful sand art. Fold an A4 paper several times, rub it around the opening of a soda can, and the soda will open by itself. This is friction-generating heat. Place a burning strip of paper into a cup, and the cooked egg placed at the opening will be swallowed inside. Just pour hot water into the bottle, and the egg will be spat out. When we fill a cup with water up to about 60%, the egg will be ready to be served. When the cup is seven-tenths full, the water stays in the cup. But if you continue to pour, you'll notice the water will flow out through a tube in the middle, even draining the previous water. This is the siphon effect. Drop a few drops of dye into an empty water bottle, fill it with hot water, then place the bottle at the bottom of a tank of cold water. You will see the dye spreads upwards with the hot water like an underwater volcano erupting. Take an empty bottle, poke a few holes around it, and you'll have a mini fountain with adjustable water flow. Stuff some scrap paper into a cup, quickly invert the cup underwater. And then lift it. The paper will still stay dry. This is the air pressure wall. Use a cotton swab dipped in vinegar to write a secret on a piece of paper, and the writing will only gradually appear after heating. This is the secret of the invisible writing. Place a glass cup in front of a girl, pour clear water into it, and you'll see the girl slowly turn around. This is the principle of water refraction. What if chewing gum sticks to your pants and won't come off? Just put an ice cube on it, and after a while, the gum will peel off easily. A single piece of paper can't bear weight. But if you fold it back and forth into a cube, it will not come off. It will come off into a corrugated shape. The paper will successfully support the weight. Do you know why this happens? Place the ends of a cotton thread into two cups. Tilt the cup with water, and the water will flow along the thread into the empty cup. This is the capillary action. Cut a potato into three small cubes. Thread them with toothpicks, and you'll have a potato balance. This is the principle of torque balance. Place a cotton thread on an ice cube. Can you believe it? Just sprinkle some salt, and you can easily lift the ice cube. This is the principle of salt melting ice. Light a piece of blotting paper. Rub the residual oil on the paper. Gently rub your fingers, and smoke will start to form. Do you know why this happens? Place an inverted glass bottle over a candle in water. Watch as the water level in the bottle rises when the candle goes out. This is the principle of air pressure difference. Cover the top of a water-filled bottle with a tissue. After wetting it and removing the excess, can you believe it? A thin piece of paper can hold the water securely inside the bottle. Don't throw away chewing gum you don't want to eat. Shape it into a cone. And while the gum isn't paying attention, use a coconut, and you're done. The coconut will actually break through it. This is the power of a non-Newtonian fluid. Put baking soda into a cup, add vinegar, and it will produce a mysterious gas. When you bring it near a burning candle, the flame will be extinguished. This is the principle of a fire extinguisher. Science is full of wonder, but it's better to experiment with the kids firsthand.

The extra top hole on running shoes is designed to create a heel lock that prevents blisters. Car headrest rods can be removed and used to break a window in an emergency. These small buttons strengthen the spots on jeans that can tear from strain. The little pom-pom on beanies wasn't just for looks. It's because sailors used it so they wouldn't hit their heads on low ceilings in ships. That little bump on your laptop charger helps stop your computer from getting noisy electronic signals. This black mesh on the microwave protects us from harmful radiation. The empty space in cup noodles protects the noodles and allows hot water to circulate. You can use a soda can tab on a hanger to make more space in a small closet.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: This is Zara, is the skincare addict with 47 serums who doesn't wake up to sunlight. She wakes up to her 12-step morning routine alarm. Her nightstand looks like a chemistry lab, crowded with droppers, toners, mists, oils, and a jade roller colder than her personality before caffeine. Every morning, she layers products like she's building emotional armor. Essence, serum, booster ampoule, then another serum for hydration. She walks into school glowing so intensely the hallway lights dim out of respect. Her friends tell her, girl, you're shiny. And she insists it's natural. Absolutely nothing about it is natural. She looks one dab away from slipping right out of her own face. In class, she can't rest her cheek on her hand because her skin is so moisturized it slides off when she turns her head. And her hair sticks to her face like flypaper from all the layers. At lunch, she pulls out sunscreen the size of a shampoo bottle and reapplies it every 12 minutes like she's in battle with the sun. People don't smell perfume on her. They smell niacinamide, hyaluronic acid, and a hint of panic. Zara isn't doing skincare. She's conducting a full scientific experiment. On her face.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: GHB. GHB is gamma-hydroxybutyrate, a central nervous system depressant that exists naturally in your brain in tiny amounts. Synthetic versions are used medically to treat narcolepsy, but recreationally it's taken as a clear, salty liquid measured in capfuls or milliliters. People use it for euphoria, lowered inhibitions, and enhanced sociability. The problem is the safe dose and the deadly dose are dangerously close. Once consumed, GHB enhances GABA, the neurotransmitter that slows brain activity and promotes relaxation. It also triggers a release of dopamine and growth hormone. The onset begins within 15 to 30 minutes. Your body loosens, anxiety melts away, and a warm wave of euphoria spreads through you. At the right dose, the peak feels like the best parts of alcohol without the sloppiness. You're social, confident, and physically relaxed. Music sounds better, touch feels heightened, and everything seems easy and flowing. But add even one extra capful and the experience flips. Speech slurs, motor control vanishes, and memory starts cutting out in chunks. Go slightly further and you're unconscious, breathing shallow, potentially slipping into a coma. The margin for error is razor thin. As the comedown hits after two to four hours, you might be able to get a sense of what's going on. You might be able to get a sense of what's going on. GHB is highly addictive, with severe physical dependence. Withdrawal causes tremors, insomnia, anxiety, and in extreme cases, seizures that require hospitalization. text_evidence.whisper_asr: Methadrone or Meow Meow is a synthetic stimulant that exploded in popularity during the late 2000s as a legal alternative to MDMA and cocaine. Nicknamed Meow Meow or MCAT, it's snorted as powder, swallowed in capsules, or occasionally injected. For a brief window, it was legal and sold openly online before governments caught up and banned it. Once consumed, Methadrone floods your brain with serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine all at once. The rush is faster than MDMA but shorter than cocaine. The onset hits within minutes if snorted. Euphoria surges through you. Energy spikes and everything feels electric and perfect. Your heart races, pupils dilate, and conversation flows endlessly. You feel invincible, social, and deeply connected to everyone around you. At the peak, the high is intense but fleeting. Music sounds incredible. Touch feels amazing. And every moment pulses with possibility. But within 30 to 60 minutes, it starts fading. That's when the trap closes. The comedown arrives fast and harsh. The euphoria vanishes, replaced by anxiety, restlessness, and an overwhelming urge to redose immediately. So you do. Then again. Then again. The compulsion to keep using is stronger than almost any other drug. Users binge for hours or days, chasing a high that gets weaker. When the supply finally runs out, the crash is brutal. Depression, paranoia, insomnia, and complete emotional exhaustion. Your brain's serotonin reserves are depleted, leaving you hollow for days.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: This is not magic but a real scientific experiment. A straw cannot penetrate an apple, but by pressing down on the top with your thumb and pushing hard, the apple will actually puncture. This is the power of air compression. How can a straw lift a bottle of water? Simply bend the straw at one-third of its length and you can lift the bottle. This uses the stability of a triangle. Don't throw away the chewing gum you don't want to eat. First mold it into a cone shape, then when the gum isn't looking, hit it with a coconut and the coconut will actually get pierced. This is the power of a non-Newtonian fluid. Sprinkle a pinch of salt on a hen's egg, then place a rooster's egg on top and you can easily make it stand up. Now take an empty bottle, punch a few holes in it, and you'll have a mini fountain with adjustable water flow. If you place a coin directly on paper, it will immediately fall, like in the video. Fold the paper, then unfold it. Place the coin on it and unfold the paper 180 degrees and the coin will not fall. It will stay stable on the paper. Pour some alcohol onto the sand, then pour a mixture of sugar and baking soda on top, ignite it, and you can create the mysterious and ancient Pharaoh's snake. A needle that can be attracted by a magnet slowly loses its magnetism after being heated. Why is this? When you put tape on the surface of a water-filled balloon and puncture the center, the water flows out as if it is frozen. This is the phenomenon of laminar flow. Place a burning strip of paper into a cup, then place a boiled egg on the bottle's opening. The egg will actually get sucked in. Simply pour hot water over the bottle and the egg will come out again. Fold an A4 paper back and forth several times. Rub a little on the opening of a cola bottle and the cola will actually open by itself. This is the heat generated by friction. What do you do if chewing gum sticks to your pants and won't come off? Simply place an ice cube and wait a little while and the gum will come off easily. Place a cotton string on an ice cube. Can you believe it? Simply sprinkle some salt and you can easily lift the ice cube. This is the principle of salt chemistry. When we pour water into a cup until it is 70% full, the water can stay inside the cup. If we continue to pour more water to fill it up, you will notice that water will start flowing out through the pipe in the center, and even the previously added water will be completely drained. This is the siphon effect of water. Science is fascinating, but it's even better to let children experience it firsthand.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: If you're listening to music in your stream, you could get in serious trouble. But I'm going to tell you exactly how to avoid that and still have a soundtrack. But there's definitely a right and a wrong way to go about it. Here's the deal. Streaming copyrighted music can lead to DMCA strikes, which are copyright strikes, muted VODs or even channel bans, if not worse. Platforms like Twitch and YouTube are cracking down hard on this. One strike might seem like nothing, but multiple strikes can get your account suspended or permanently banned. Your content, your community, gone, and it's just not worth that risk in my personal opinion. But luckily, I do have solutions to this. The first solution is using services with licenses. Things like Monstercat Gold, Pretzel Rocks, Epidemic Sound. These platforms give you stream-safe music with proper licensing. Now you do have to pay a subscription for these, but it does mean that you're fully protected. And here's solution number two, but I would recommend using this alongside the first one and not instead of. Using separate audio channels in your streaming software. Set up one channel for music that doesn't save to VODs or clips. This way, your live viewers hear the music, but your archived content stays safe from copyright claims. This is also super useful when it comes to editing clips. Here's how to do it. In OBS, go to your settings, head to the audio and enable multiple audio tracks. Assign your music to track 2, and in your recording or streaming settings, only save track 1 to VODs. It takes 5 minutes to set up and it saves you from massive headaches. Don't risk your channel over a playlist. Get licensed music or separate your audio tracks, or ideally, both. Your future self will really thank you. Share this with a streamer. Remember that you want to help stay out of trouble. Save this video and follow for more streaming tips. If this has been useful to you, please leave a comment and make sure you follow.

text_evidence.whisper_asr: Pour a little phosphorus-containing laundry detergent onto a tissue, roll the tissue into a tube, rub it back and forth with your slipper, then pick it up and gently blow on it, and the tissue catches fire. What should you do if there is a power outage at home? Just add rice into a cup, pour in some clean water, add a little cooking oil, insert a cotton swab in the center, and light it, and you will get a candle that can burn for a long time. Fill a basin with clean water, put a mirror inside it, adjust the angle, and you will get a moving rainbow. Use sandpaper to remove the paint from a soda can, hang the can over an empty cup with a wooden stick, pour drain cleaner into the cup, wait for a while, then take it out, and you will find the can has become transparent. Pour different amounts of water into three or four cups. How can you evenly distribute the water into all four cups? Just place a bent straw filled with water between two cups, and you will see the water automatically distribute into all four cups until it balances. This is the siphon effect. Draw a circle on the pan with garlic, and the fried egg will turn out perfectly round. Apply a layer of water. Apply a layer of water. Put a little garlic juice on your fingers, and you can easily lift the egg yolk without breaking it. This is a non-Newtonian fluid effect. Put a burning strip of paper into a glass bottle, then place a boiled egg on the bottle mouth, and the egg is sucked inside. Just pour hot water over the bottom of the bottle, and the egg comes back out. This is atmospheric pressure. What happens if you add milk into cola? Tighten the bottle cap and wait for a while. The cola actually becomes clear. Would you still dare to drink it after seeing this? Cut the foil paper from chewing gum into strips. Connect both ends to the positive. If you have a bottle cap, you can see the positive and negative sides of a battery, and you can survive outdoors. Rub a glass cup around the mouth of a beer bottle a few times. Tap it lightly, and the beer will spray out. Keep dripping water onto a coin, protected by surface tension. Count how many drops you can add at most. What should you do if you can't open a jar? Turn the jar upside down in hot water. Wait for one minute, and it will open easily. If the Sprite pull ring breaks, don't panic. Keep rubbing chopsticks around the can opening, and it will open by itself. This is heat generated by friction. Instead of letting children watch virtual fun, phones and TVs, it's better to let them watch real and practical science knowledge.

How assessments work? text_evidence.whisper_asr: My biggest tips on how to spend winter break productively in high school as someone who got a 4.0 taking all APs and also got into five IVs. So I love winter break. I loved all of the breaks so much in high school because literally it is just a time to relax, reset, get ahead, and ultimately make it so that you are so much less stressed in the time to come. Sure, you could totally leave off beginning your classes, starting everything, getting all of your foundations set until the first day, the first week, the first month. However, that is so stressful. That leaves all of the stress to yourself in the moment when you're trying to juggle everything going on. And if you're a very high achieving student, if you're trying to get into IVs, if you're trying to get all A's, you're already under so much stress. Why don't you just set the foundations beforehand when you're not as stressed, when you really don't have anything on your plate so that the time can be so much easier for you and you can just focus on the academics. So that's why I loved winter break so much. How I spent it when I was in high school was that I would always get ahead. Whether your classes are semester long or year long, you can either get ahead on the content and the classes that you know that you're going to have in the spring or just get an extra unit ahead if your classes are year long and you already have the textbook, already know the way that your teacher structures the class, know everything basically. So that's tip one. Make sure you're getting at least one unit ahead. The second thing I always like to do, and I don't care who thinks this is crazy, I would map out the entirety of what my spring semester would look like. You're able to look back at the fall semester and see, okay, take a class like APUSH. When did my teacher give me tests for APUSH? I don't exactly remember, but I'll say we had around one every three weeks. That means that similarly, most likely you're going to have one around every three weeks your spring semester. I did that for all of my classes. I would project I would ask my teachers for schedules beforehand. I started doing that junior year, sophomore year was all just estimation because I was too embarrassed to ask. So you can either estimate if you're embarrassed or actually ask. But the best thing was I was able to see what would each of my weeks look like and what were my hell weeks. Hell weeks were weeks where my extracurriculars hit really hard and so did academics. But the best thing was I had planned for that. So the week before, I always knew what week before hell week would come. Because I had it marked in my calendar. And a week before that, I would just start pre-learning some content. I would just get ahead again. And literally, this kept me from experiencing so much stress in high school. Because I was just always on top of things. I was always ahead. And people always ask me how I slept or when I slept. This was how I slept. I am telling you, sleep was one of the most important things for me in high school. Because you need good foundations. And sleep is a foundation. Health is a foundation. You need to be sleeping. You need to be eating. You need to be eating. You need to be doing all of the right things and treating yourself correctly so that your brain can function properly. So that you can function properly and ultimately be able to get the straight A's that you're looking for. Literally, if you have good life foundations, I believe that everything becomes a lot easier. Because if you're not sleeping, like there's no way. There's no way for you to make it through. So that's my second tip project. I would, I like drawing my own. I would do this every break. But I would make my own calendars that was just like a creative thing for me. And then I would draw right out my weeks what they would look like. I'm gonna make a part two because I have a lot more tips. But this ended up being kind of long. You can comment any questions you have and follow me for more academic and study tips. Bye!
